## Set-up

```{r set up 1, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
options(scipen = 999)
```

```{r set up 2, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(igraph)
library(sf)
```

## Source 1: census tract → neighbourhood bridge table

**Dataset comments**:

This block builds the relationship between census tracts and neighbourhoods. The neighbourhood is a stable unit of analysis for the whole study period except for three known exceptions dated in 2017 (see Note). Census tracts, on the other hand, are not stable over time, so a fixed crosswalk loses a growing fraction of population the further away the crosswalk's reference date is from 2024 (empirically checked against `composición_hogares/` 2017-2025).

Note: 2017 has 128 neighbourhoods, not 131: Ensanche de Vallecas, Valderrivas and El Cañaveral did not exist as neighbourhoods of their own as of January 1st, 2017 - their census tracts belonged to Villa de Vallecas/Vicálvaro.

### Dataset cleaning

#### Source 1a: neighbourhood names (`seccion_censal_barrio_correspondencia.xls`)

`seccion_censal_barrio_correspondencia.xls` is used only to obtain district/neighbourhood names (not to build the tract-neighbourhood relationship, since it has two transcription omissions: tracts 10220 and 16137)

```{r fuente 1a, message=FALSE}
nbsp <- " " # Stores in a variable the NBSP character (non-breaking space) since many cells carry it by default.

raw_corr <-
  read_excel("../data/raw/seccion_censal_barrio_correspondencia.xls", sheet = 1,
             col_names = FALSE) %>% # marks that the first column is data, not a header
  rename(etiqueta = ...1) %>% # renames that first column ...1 to "etiqueta".
  mutate(
      etiqueta = str_squish(str_replace_all(etiqueta, nbsp, " ")),
      # str_replace_all replaces every NBSP with a normal space and str_squish trims spaces and collapses multiple internal spaces into one.

      # main difference: district row: "01. CENTRO" (period + space); neighbourhood row: "01.1 Palacio" (period + digit)
      es_distrito = str_detect(etiqueta, "^\\d{2}\\.\\s"),
      es_barrio   = str_detect(etiqueta, "^\\d{2}\\.\\d+\\s"))

distritos <- raw_corr %>%
  filter(es_distrito) %>% 
  transmute( 
    distrito_num = as.integer(str_extract(etiqueta, "^\\d{2}")), # extracts the first two digits and converts them to integer (drops the leading zero, e.g. "01" → 1).
    distrito_nombre = str_remove(etiqueta, "^\\d{2}\\.\\s*") %>% # Removes the "01. " prefix (digits, period, spaces).
      str_replace_all("\\s*\\.\\s*", "-") %>% # turns " . " into a hyphen
      str_to_title() %>% # converts to title case (initial capital on each word): "San Blas-Canillejas".
      str_replace_all("\\bDe\\b", "de") # Since str_to_title() also capitalizes prepositions like "de", this lowercases them again, giving "de la Concepción".
  )

barrios_madrid <- raw_corr %>%
  filter(es_barrio) %>%
  transmute(
    distrito_num = as.integer(str_extract(etiqueta, "^\\d{2}")), 
    barrio_num   = as.integer(str_extract(etiqueta, "(?<=^\\d{2}\\.)\\d+")), # uses a lookbehind (?<=^\\d{2}\\.)\\d+ — extracts the digits that come right after "two digits + period" at the start, without including those two digits or the period in the result.
    barrio_nombre = str_trim(str_remove(etiqueta, "^\\d{2}\\.\\d+\\s*")), # removes the "01.1 " prefix and trims leftover spaces
    barrio_oficial = distrito_num*10 + barrio_num, # building the neighbourhood-district code as it appears in some files
    codigo_barrio = sprintf("%02d%d", distrito_num, barrio_num) # building the neighbourhood-district code as it appears in other  files = DDB format (2-digit district + neighbourhood without zeros), e.g. "014" = Justicia
  ) %>%
  left_join(distritos, by = "distrito_num") %>% # for each row of the neighbourhood table, looks up in distritos the row with the same distrito_num.
  select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, barrio_oficial) %>%
  arrange(distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

#### Source 1b: sectioning history (`historia_secciones.xls`)

`historia_secciones.xls` is the 1988-2024 history of each tract code: when it was registered or deregistered, which tract it came from if it was born from a split (`procedencia`), which tract it was absorbed into if it was merged (`destino`), and whether it changed neighbourhood while keeping its number (`barrio_antiguo` + `fecha_modificacion`). It is the source of the tract-neighbourhood relationship and allows reconstructing it for any year.

```{r fuente 1b, message=FALSE}
historia <- read_excel("../data/raw/historia_secciones.xls", sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE) %>%
  rename(distrito = ...1, barrio_registrado = ...2, seccion = ...3,
         fecha_alta = ...4, procedencia = ...5, fecha_baja = ...6,
         destino = ...7, fecha_modificacion = ...8,
         barrio_antiguo = ...9, observaciones = ...10) %>%

  mutate(across(everything(), ~ str_squish(str_replace_all(as.character(.x), nbsp, " ")))) %>% # applies the same cleaning function (~ is shorthand for function (.x)) to all columns at once: converts each column to text > replaces NBSP with normal spaces > trims spaces and collapses multiple internal spaces.

  filter(str_detect(distrito, "^\\d+$")) %>% # Keeps only the rows where the distrito column is exclusively digits, so it drops header and footer.

  mutate(
    distrito = as.integer(distrito),
    barrio_registrado = as.integer(barrio_registrado),
    seccion = as.integer(seccion),
    barrio_antiguo = as.integer(barrio_antiguo),
    fecha_alta = as.integer(fecha_alta), # dates are converted to integer because in the excel they are encoded in YYYYMMDD format
    fecha_baja = as.integer(fecha_baja),
    fecha_modificacion = as.integer(fecha_modificacion)
  )
```

#### Neighbourhood-tract at a reference date

```{r neighbourhood vigente}
# Used to answer "given a census tract code, which neighbourhood did it belong to on a specific date?"
crosswalk_a_fecha <- function(historia, fecha_ref) {
  historia %>%

    filter(fecha_alta <= fecha_ref) %>% # keeps only the tracts that already existed at fecha_ref, whose registration date is earlier than the reference date...
    filter(is.na(fecha_baja) | fecha_baja > fecha_ref) %>% # ...and that have not been deregistered (either no deregistration date, OR a deregistration date later than the reference date).

    mutate(
      barrio_oficial = if_else( # determines which neighbourhood each tract belonged to at each fecha_ref
        !is.na(fecha_modificacion) & !is.na(barrio_antiguo) & fecha_ref < fecha_modificacion,
        # if this tract did have a registered neighbourhood change (fecha_modificacion AND barrio_antiguo are not empty), AND the reference date being queried is earlier than when that change happened...
        barrio_antiguo, # TRUE: the change had not happened yet (date earlier than fecha_ref) = returns the previous neighbourhood (from the barrio_antiguo column).
        barrio_registrado  # FALSE: the change has already happened (date later than fecha_ref) = returns the current neighbourhood (from the barrio_registrado column).
    )) %>%
    transmute(distrito, seccion, barrio_oficial)
}
```

#### Source 1c: year-by-year tract-neighbourhood crosswalk

The tract-neighbourhood relationship is rebuilt as of January 1st of each year in the study period and joined with `barrios_madrid` to bring in the names.

```{r fuente 1c}
anios_estudio_plus <- 2017:2025

crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio <- map_dfr(anios_estudio_plus, function(anio) { # aplies the function to each year and combines all the results 
  crosswalk_a_fecha(historia, as.integer(paste0(anio, "0101"))) %>% mutate(anio = anio) # pastes the year together with the text "0101" to form a date in YYYYMMDD format, stores it as integer, calls the function, and with mutate adds a new anio column with the value of the year being processed in that iteration.
}) %>%

  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% select(barrio_oficial, barrio_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
            by = "barrio_oficial") %>% # joins the previous table with barrios_madrid to bring in the names (district and neighbourhood) and codigo_barrio, using barrio_oficial as the key.

  mutate(codigo_seccion = sprintf("%02d%03d", distrito, seccion)) %>% # Creates a census tract code as text, combining district (2 digits) and tract (3 digits) - both zero-padded as needed.

  transmute(anio, distrito_num = distrito, distrito_nombre, barrio_num,
            barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, barrio_oficial, seccion_num = seccion, codigo_seccion) %>% 
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num, seccion_num)
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 1, message=FALSE}
# checks how many rows the barrios_madrid table has -> 131
stopifnot(nrow(barrios_madrid) == 131)

# checks that for each row of `historia` the district matches what can be recalculated from barrio_registrado -> internal consistency between two columns that should be aligned
stopifnot(all(historia$distrito == historia$barrio_registrado %/% 10))

# checks how many census tracts the official file has -> 2462
secciones_2024 <- read_excel("../data/raw/secciones_2024.xls", sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE) %>%
  rename(distrito = ...1, barrio_oficial = ...2, seccion = ...3) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
  filter(str_detect(distrito, "^\\d+$")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.integer))
stopifnot(nrow(secciones_2024) == 2462)

# checks that the district-tract-neighbourhood combinations are identical between both tables
# anti_join returns the rows of A that have no equivalent row in B: diff1 are the rows the reconstruction generates incorrectly relative to the official table, and diff2 are the rows of the official table that the reconstruction fails to generate.
cw_20241015 <- crosswalk_a_fecha(historia, 20241015)
diff1 <- anti_join(cw_20241015, secciones_2024, by = c("distrito", "seccion", "barrio_oficial"))
diff2 <- anti_join(secciones_2024, cw_20241015, by = c("distrito", "seccion", "barrio_oficial"))
stopifnot(nrow(diff1) == 0, nrow(diff2) == 0)

# checks that no crosswalk row was left without a neighbourhood name (join failure).
stopifnot(sum(is.na(crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio$barrio_nombre)) == 0)

# checks there are no duplicates (e.g. a census tract with two neighbourhoods)
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_seccion))) == 0)

# exploratory: extracts the unique neighbourhoods of 2017 and of 2018, and uses anti_join() to find which neighbourhoods are in 2018 but not in 2017.
barrios_2017 <- crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio %>% filter(anio == 2017) %>% distinct(barrio_oficial)
barrios_2018 <- crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio %>% filter(anio == 2018) %>% distinct(barrio_oficial, barrio_nombre)
barrios_2018 %>% anti_join(barrios_2017, by = "barrio_oficial")
```

## Source 2: household composition (`composición_hogares/`)

**Dataset comments**:

The source is at census-tract level, so it uses the crosswalk. The 9 variables to be built detail different household compositions (detailed in columnas_objetivo) and will be the count and percentage of the number of households with such compositions: A single woman aged 16 to 64 + a single man aged 16 to 64, Two adults aged 16 to 64, with no children, Two adults and one child, Two adults and two children, Two adults and three or more children, An adult woman with one or more children, An adult man with one or more children.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 2}
# Lists the column names to use to locate them by text match.

columnas_objetivo <- c(
  "Total",
  "Una mujer sola de 16 a 64 años",
  "Un hombre solo de 16 a 64 años",
  "Dos adultos de 16 a 64 años, sin menores",
  "Dos adultos y un menor",
  "Dos adultos y dos menores",
  "Dos adultos y tres o más menores",
  "Una mujer adulta con uno o más menores",
  "Un hombre adulto con uno o más menores"
)

nombres_finales <- c(
  "total_hogares", "hog_mujer_sola_16_64", "hog_hombre_solo_16_64",
  "hog_dos_adultos_sin_menores", "hog_dos_adultos_1_menor", "hog_dos_adultos_2_menores",
  "hog_dos_adultos_3mas_menores", "hog_mujer_adulta_con_menores", "hog_hombre_adulto_con_menores"
)
```

```{r parse 2}
parse_num <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x) # converts x (the column vector) to text so transformations can be applied, then stores it as numeric.
  x <- if_else(x == "..", NA_character_, x) # wherever ".." appears writes NA, and keeps the values of x everywhere else
  x <- str_remove_all(x, "\\.") # removes the thousands-separator periods
  as.numeric(x)
}
```

#### Reading per year

```{r lectura 2}
leer_composicion_anio <- function(anio) { # Defines a function that takes a year (anio) and returns that year's household composition data 

  archivo <- list.files("../data/raw/composición_hogares",
                        pattern = paste0("^", anio, "_hogares\\.xlsx?$"), full.names = TRUE) # Looks within the folder for the file whose name exactly matches the pattern: year followed by _hogares.xlsx or _hogares.xls.
             stopifnot(length(archivo) == 1) # warns if more than one file matches that pattern, or none


  hojas <- excel_sheets(archivo) # lists the names of every sheet that excel file has
  hoja_comp <- hojas[str_detect(str_to_lower(hojas), "composici")] # looks for the one with "composici" in lowercase (saves having to match the accent).
  stopifnot(length(hoja_comp) == 1) # warns if more than one sheet matches that pattern, or none


  raw <- read_excel(archivo, sheet = hoja_comp, col_names = FALSE) # reads the composition sheet, without assuming a header row
  cabecera_limpia <- str_to_lower(str_squish(coalesce(as.character(raw[6, ]), as.character(raw[5, ])))) # extracts row 6 (or failing that row 5) in full (where the column names are), converts it to lowercase text and applies str_squish to clean up spaces - the result is a text vector in order.
  objetivo_limpio <- str_to_lower(str_squish(columnas_objetivo))


  idx <- match(objetivo_limpio, cabecera_limpia)
  names(idx) <- columnas_objetivo # assigns the original name to each of the 9 numbers in the idx vector - in order.

 if (any(is.na(idx))) { # checks whether there is at least one TRUE in the vector generated by is.na(idx)
  stop(sprintf("Year %d: there is a column-matching error: %s",
               anio, paste(columnas_objetivo[is.na(idx)], collapse = "; "))) 
 }

  col_seccion <- str_squish(as.character(raw[[2]])) # col2 = tract code
  es_seccion <- replace_na(str_detect(col_seccion, "^\\d{5}$"), FALSE) # str_detect identifies the rows that are a census tract, discarding header, total or empty rows - the result is a TRUE/FALSE/NA vector. replace_na(..., FALSE) replaces any NA that might come out (if some cell was empty) with FALSE - the result is a TRUE/FALSE vector.

  datos <- raw[es_seccion, ] # filters the raw table keeping only the rows where es_seccion is TRUE (by convention) - the ones that are census tracts.
  codigo_seccion <- col_seccion[es_seccion] # applies the same filter to the col_seccion vector


  valores <- tibble(.rows = nrow(datos)) # creates an empty table with the number of rows that "datos" has
  for (i in seq_along(idx)) {
  valores[[nombres_finales[i]]] <- parse_num(datos[[idx[i]]]) # datos[idx[i]] extracts from "datos" the excel column position corresponding to category number i, cleans it with the parse_num defined earlier, and stores it inside valores under the name corresponding to position i of nombres_finales.
}

  bind_cols(tibble(codigo_seccion = codigo_seccion), valores) %>% mutate(anio = anio) # joins the tract-code table and the values table - one table next to the other - adding the year (anio) column.
}
```

```{r resultados 2, message=FALSE}
resultados_hogares <- map(anios_estudio_plus, leer_composicion_anio) # calls the function - the result of map() is a list of 9 elements.
composicion_seccion <- bind_rows(resultados_hogares) # walks through that list of 9 tables and stacks them one below the other, producing the final table.
```

#### Join with the year-by-year crosswalk

```{r union 2}
# A left_join is done, starting from the household composition table which is joined against crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio

composicion_join <- composicion_seccion %>%
  left_join(
    crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio %>%
      select(anio, codigo_seccion, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
    by = c("anio", "codigo_seccion"))
```

#### Aggregation to neighbourhood level

```{r agreg 2}
# from census-tract level to neighbourhood level
composicion_hogares_barrio_anio <- composicion_join %>%
  group_by(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(nombres_finales), sum), .groups = "drop") %>% # computes the sum of the values for the census tracts within the neighbourhoods
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 2}
# checks there are no duplicate tracts
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(composicion_seccion %>% select(anio, codigo_seccion))) == 0)

# checks that no census tract is missing relative to the already-validated crosswalk count
secciones_leidas <- composicion_seccion %>% distinct(anio, codigo_seccion) %>% count(anio, name = "n_leidas")
secciones_esperadas <- crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio %>% distinct(anio, codigo_seccion) %>% count(anio, name = "n_esperadas")
comparacion_secciones <- left_join(secciones_leidas, secciones_esperadas, by = "anio")
stopifnot(all(comparacion_secciones$n_leidas == comparacion_secciones$n_esperadas))

# checks that no row of composicion_join was left without its corresponding neighbourhood after the join
stopifnot(sum(is.na(composicion_join$barrio_nombre)) == 0)

# checks how many distinct neighbourhoods appear registered in each year (128 in 2017 and 131 in the rest)
barrios_por_anio_hogares <- composicion_hogares_barrio_anio %>% distinct(anio, barrio_nombre) %>% count(anio, name = "n_barrios")
stopifnot(all(barrios_por_anio_hogares$n_barrios[barrios_por_anio_hogares$anio == 2017] == 128))
stopifnot(all(barrios_por_anio_hogares$n_barrios[barrios_por_anio_hogares$anio != 2017] == 131))
```


## Source 3: rent (`alquiler_barrio.xlsx`)

**Dataset comments**:

The variables extracted are: average rent for multi-family housing, average rent for single-family housing, number of multi-family housing units, and number of single-family housing units. The source is at census-tract level, so each year it is joined with the crosswalk, with some variations. The `alquiler_barrio.xlsx` file is not always published with the tract geography in effect as of January 1st of the year indicated by the sheet name. There are two mismatch cases: the "2017" sheet already uses tract codes that administratively did not exist until after January 1st, 2017, and the "2023" sheet uses 2022 geography. An empirical check concludes that using the 2018 crosswalk to read the "2017" sheet, and the 2022 crosswalk to read the "2023" sheet, brings tracts left without an assigned neighbourhood down to 0%.

```{r cw 3}
anio_crosswalk_alquiler <- c(
  "2017" = 2018, "2018" = 2018, "2019" = 2019, "2020" = 2020, "2021" = 2021,
  "2022" = 2022, "2023" = 2022)
```

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 3}
# vector to name the columns in the Excel

columnas_alquiler_objetivo <- c(
  grupo_colectiva = "Renta media vivienda colectiva",
  grupo_unifamiliar = "Renta media vivienda unifamiliar",
  n_colectiva = "Viviendas colectivas",
  n_unifamiliar = "Viviendas unifamiliares"
)

# Converts to text, replaces ".." with NA, converts to number
parse_num_alquiler <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- if_else(x == "..", NA_character_, x)
  as.numeric(x)
}
```

#### Reading per year

A prior detection of the fixed column positions to use is carried out. Row and column layout verified across every sheet of the file, knowing that the "data range" starts at row 2.

```{r lectura 3, message=FALSE}
# Reads the sheet corresponding to the year
leer_alquiler_anio <- function(anio) {
  archivo <- "../data/raw/alquiler_barrio.xlsx"
  raw_alquiler <- read_excel(archivo, sheet = as.character(anio), col_names = FALSE) # without assuming an automatic header

# Verification of the variables at fixed positions determined within the excel
# Each stopifnot compares the text of a specific cell (raw[row, column], cleaned with str_squish) against the corresponding entry of the columnas_alquiler_objetivo vector
stopifnot(str_squish(as.character(raw_alquiler[3, 8])) == columnas_alquiler_objetivo["grupo_colectiva"])
stopifnot(str_squish(as.character(raw_alquiler[3, 17])) == columnas_alquiler_objetivo["grupo_unifamiliar"])
stopifnot(str_squish(as.character(raw_alquiler[5, 3])) == columnas_alquiler_objetivo["n_colectiva"])
stopifnot(str_squish(as.character(raw_alquiler[5, 4])) == columnas_alquiler_objetivo["n_unifamiliar"])

# Example: if you are processing sheet "2017", as.character(anio) converts it to text "2017", and anio_crosswalk_map_alquiler[["2017"]] looks up that key in the dictionary and returns the associated value (2018).
anio_cw <- anio_crosswalk_alquiler[[as.character(anio)]]

# Renames each column with a useful name
raw_alquiler <- raw_alquiler %>% rename(
    codigo_seccion = ...1,
    n_viviendas_colectiva = ...3,
    n_viviendas_unifamiliar = ...4,
    renta_colectiva_mediana = ...8,
    renta_unifamiliar_mediana = ...17,) %>%

    mutate(codigo_seccion = str_squish(as.character(codigo_seccion))) %>% # cleans up spaces
    filter(str_detect(codigo_seccion, "^\\d{5}$")) # filters by the 5-digit pattern (tracts), dropping unneeded rows

# Builds the final table with the columns year, crosswalk-year, tract code and 4 cleaned numeric variables.
raw_alquiler %>%
    transmute(
      anio = anio,
      anio_crosswalk = anio_cw,
      codigo_seccion,
      n_viviendas_colectiva = parse_num_alquiler(n_viviendas_colectiva),
      n_viviendas_unifamiliar = parse_num_alquiler(n_viviendas_unifamiliar),
      renta_colectiva_mediana = parse_num_alquiler(renta_colectiva_mediana),
      renta_unifamiliar_mediana = parse_num_alquiler(renta_unifamiliar_mediana),
    )
}

# runs the function for every year and stacks the results
anios_estudio_alquiler <- 2017:2023
alquiler_seccion <- map_dfr(anios_estudio_alquiler, leer_alquiler_anio) # walks through the anios_estudio_alquiler vector and for each one calls the leer_alquiler_anio function. Each call returns its own table and they are stacked directly one below the other.
```

#### Join with the year-by-year crosswalk

```{r union 3}
# A left_join is done, starting from the neighbourhood rent table which is joined against crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio

alquiler_join <- alquiler_seccion %>%
  left_join(
    crosswalk_seccion_barrio_por_anio %>%
      select(anio, codigo_seccion, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
    by = c("anio_crosswalk" = "anio", "codigo_seccion")
  )
```

#### (Weighted) aggregation to neighbourhood level

To summarize several tracts into a single neighbourhood figure, the chosen approach was to compute the weighted mean of the tract-level medians, which gives each tract a "weight" proportional to its size (the number of dwellings). Since individual dwelling-level data is not available to extract their median directly, this measure was chosen to approximate it.

```{r agreg 3}
# Defines the function, with x (the values, the rent medians per tract) and w (the weights, the number of dwellings per tract)

weighted_mean_safe <- function(x, w) {
  # checks to make it robust (safe)
  valido <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w) & w > 0 # the value cannot be missing & the weight cannot be missing & weight > 0
  if (!any(valido)) return(NA_real_) # if no tract of the neighbourhood is usable returns NA // if at least one is valid, applies the following weighted-mean operation to them:
  sum(x[valido] * w[valido]) / sum(w[valido]) # MEAN: multiplies the value by its weight, sums everything and divides by the sum of the weights.
}


# Aggregation by neighbourhood

alquiler_barrio_anio <- alquiler_join %>%
  group_by(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio) %>% # grouped by several columns to avoid losing information.

  summarise(
    # Dwelling counts are summed directly, without weighting, ignoring NAs when summing.
    n_viviendas_colectiva_barrio = sum(n_viviendas_colectiva, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_viviendas_unifamiliar_barrio = sum(n_viviendas_unifamiliar, na.rm = TRUE),

    # The median rent values have the weighted mean applied to them (function above)
    renta_colectiva_barrio = weighted_mean_safe(renta_colectiva_mediana, n_viviendas_colectiva),
    renta_unifamiliar_barrio = weighted_mean_safe(renta_unifamiliar_mediana, n_viviendas_unifamiliar),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num) # Sorts the final table by year, district and neighbourhood
```

Tract 10157, which corresponds to the neighbourhood of Campamento in the Latina district, has no data in this `alquiler_barrio` file.

In `renta_colectiva_barrio`, El Cañaveral in 2017 is NA since that neighbourhood was created in November 2017 (see Source 1), so in its first year it barely had a registered rental stock and the Ayuntamiento censors the price for statistical confidentiality.

`renta_unifamiliar_mediana` has a high rate of non-random NAs, since 73% of the NAs (540 of 736) are censorship due to statistical confidentiality. That is, there are single-family dwellings in that neighbourhood-year but none of its tracts have a published price because the sample within the tract is too small. Even so, the single-family dwelling variables are kept in the initial dataset.

```{r MAR}

  mutate(
    motivo_na_unifamiliar = case_when(

      TRUE ~ "single-family dwelling exists but price censored (statistical confidentiality)"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(motivo_na_unifamiliar)
```

## Source 4: declared housing price (`precio_vivienda_declarado_actualizado.xlsx`)

**Dataset comments**:

The extracted variable is the reported housing price. This dataset is at neighbourhood level and in long format. Coverage rate (source limitation): the file's footer states that the Colegio de Registradores captures between 95.3% (2020) and 98.4% (2019) of the actual transactions each year. NA sentinel: some neighbourhood-years have the price as "0,00"; the file's footer explains that "the figure is only shown per neighbourhood when a minimum of 15 cases is available", this is the NA sentinel for statistical confidentiality.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r liimpieza 4, message=FALSE}
precio_vivienda_declarado_raw <- read_excel("../data/raw/precio_vivienda_declarado_actualizado.xlsx",
                                             sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE) %>% # reads the excel sheet without assuming a header row
  rename(anio = ...1, distrito_txt = ...2, barrio_txt = ...3, precio_txt = ...4) %>% # renames the 4 columns

  filter(str_detect(anio, "^\\d{4}$")) %>% # keeps only the rows where anio is exactly 4 digits, discarding any header row, footnotes, etc.
  filter(barrio_txt != distrito_txt & # discards the rows where the text of column 2 and 3 is equal (district total and city) AND...
           str_detect(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}\\.\\s")) # ...AND requires barrio_txt to start with "3 digits + period + space"


parse_precio_declarado <- function(x) { # defines the cleaning function
  x <- str_remove_all(x, "\\.") # removes the periods (thousands separator)
  x <- str_replace(x, ",", ".") # replaces the decimal comma with a decimal period
  x <- as.numeric(x) # converts to number
  if_else(x == 0, NA_real_, x) # converts to NA since "0,00" = sentinel for <15 transactions, not a real price.
}

precio_vivienda_declarado_barrio_anio <- precio_vivienda_declarado_raw %>%
  transmute( # creates the final columns, dropping the rest
    anio = as.integer(anio),
    codigo_barrio_vivienda  = str_extract(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}"), # extracts the first 3 digits from the neighbourhood text.
    precio_vivienda_declarado_barrio = parse_precio_declarado(precio_txt) # applies the cleaning function to the price
  ) %>%

  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
            by = c("codigo_barrio_vivienda" = "codigo_barrio")) %>% # joins this table with barrios_madrid, bringing in the rest of the neighbourhood information, matching on codigo_barrio (already created).

  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio = codigo_barrio_vivienda, precio_vivienda_declarado_barrio) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

## Source 5: income (`rentas_barrio.csv`)

**Dataset comments**:

The extracted variables are average gross household income, average gross income per person average net household income and average net income per person. This dataset is at neighbourhood level and in long format. Confirmed directly in the raw file, it was found that at neighbourhood level, `Renta bruta media por hogar` is identical to `Renta neta media por hogar` in every row. At district and city level they are indeed different. `Renta bruta/neta media por persona` are correctly differentiated at neighbourhood level.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rentas_raw <- read_delim("../data/raw/rentas_barrio.csv", delim = ";", 
                          locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
                          skip = 4, col_names = TRUE, # the header starts after skipping 4 rows
                          col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) |> # forces the columns to text; otherwise the "." (from "21.570") would be read as a decimal and we want it to arrive intact before applying the parse cleaning

rename(anio_txt = ...1, distrito_txt = ...2, barrio_txt = ...3) # renaming the first 3 columns

rentas_datos <- rentas_raw %>%
  filter(str_detect(anio_txt, "^\\d{4}$")) %>% # only rows where anio_txt is 4 digits
  filter(as.integer(anio_txt) <= 2023) %>% # only the ones ≤2023
  filter(str_detect(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}\\.\\s")) # only rows where barrio_txt has the "3 digits + period + space" pattern at the start, discarding the district-total and city rows.

parse_renta <- function(x) as.numeric(str_remove_all(x, "\\.")) # since these are integers with no decimals, only the thousands-separator periods are removed

rentas_barrio_anio <- rentas_datos %>% # builds the final columns (cleaning the originals with parse_renta)
  transmute(
    anio = as.integer(anio_txt),
    codigo_barrio = str_extract(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}"), # codigo_barrio extracted from the first 3 digits
    renta_neta_media_persona = parse_renta(`Renta neta media por persona`),
    renta_neta_media_hogar = parse_renta(`Renta neta media por hogar`),
    renta_bruta_media_persona = parse_renta(`Renta bruta media por persona`),
    renta_bruta_media_hogar = parse_renta(`Renta bruta media por hogar`)
  ) %>%

  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
            by = "codigo_barrio") %>% # joins this table with barrios_madrid, bringing in the rest of the neighbourhood information, matching on codigo_barrio (already created)
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, renta_neta_media_persona,
         renta_neta_media_hogar, renta_bruta_media_persona, renta_bruta_media_hogar) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

```{r compro 5}
# checks there are no duplicate neighbourhoods
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(rentas_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio))) == 0)

# checks whether there are NAs - since this dataset has no declared sentinel.
stopifnot(sum(is.na(select(rentas_barrio_anio, starts_with("renta")))) == 0)

# checks that gross income is never lower than net income (gross >= net)
check_bruta_neta <- function(bruta, neta) {
  stopifnot(sum(bruta < neta, na.rm = TRUE) == 0)
}
check_bruta_neta(rentas_barrio_anio$renta_bruta_media_persona, rentas_barrio_anio$renta_neta_media_persona)
check_bruta_neta(rentas_barrio_anio$renta_bruta_media_hogar, rentas_barrio_anio$renta_neta_media_hogar)
```

## Source 6: age bracket (`tramo_edad/`)

**Dataset comments**:

This dataset is at neighbourhood level. From this source only the age indicator of the gentrification index is needed (% population aged 25-39). The results are computed as a value from 0 to 1.


### Dataset cleaning

```{r parse 6}
parse_num_edad <- function(x) as.numeric(str_remove_all(x, "\\.")) # removes the thousands-separator period.
```

#### Reading per year

```{r lectura 6, message=FALSE}
leer_tramo_edad_anio <- function(anio) { # Defines a function that takes a year (anio) and returns that year's age-bracket data already processed.
  archivo <- list.files("../data/raw/tramo_edad",
                         pattern = paste0("^", anio, "_tramo_edad\\.xlsx$"), full.names = TRUE) # Looks within the folder for the file whose name exactly matches the pattern: year followed by _tramo_edad.xlsx or _tramo_edad.xls.
  stopifnot(length(archivo) == 1) # warns if more than one file matches that pattern, or none.


  raw_edad <- read_excel(archivo, sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE) # reads the first sheet without assuming an automatic header.

  raw_edad %>%
    rename(distrito_txt = ...1, barrio_txt = ...2, tramo = ...3, poblacion_col = ...4) %>% # Renames the first 4 columns by position
    filter(distrito_txt != "Total" & !(barrio_txt %in% c("Total", "NO CONSTA"))) %>% # discards the city block, the district-total blocks and "no consta" (population without an assigned neighbourhood)
    filter(tramo %in% c("Total", "25 - 29", "30 - 34", "35 - 39")) %>% 
    transmute( # Builds that year's final table
      anio = anio,
      distrito_txt = str_squish(distrito_txt), # cleans up spaces
      barrio_txt = str_squish(barrio_txt),
      tramo = case_match(tramo, "Total" ~ "poblacion_total_barrio", "25 - 29" ~ "pob_25_29", "30 - 34" ~ "pob_30_34", "35 - 39" ~ "pob_35_39"), 
      poblacion = parse_num_edad(poblacion_col)) # cleans and converts the population to a number.
}

# runs the function for every year and stacks the results
anios_estudio_edad <- 2017:2023
tramo_edad_largo <- map_dfr(anios_estudio_edad, leer_tramo_edad_anio) # walks through the anios_estudio_edad vector and for each one calls the leer_tramo_edad_anio function.
```

#### To wide format and computing the indicator

```{r ancho 6}
tramo_edad_ancho <- tramo_edad_largo %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = tramo, values_from = poblacion) %>% # one row per neighbourhood-year, one column per bracket
  mutate(
    pob_25_39_barrio = pob_25_29 + pob_30_34 + pob_35_39,
    pct_pob_25_39 = pob_25_39_barrio / poblacion_total_barrio # and its % of the total is computed
  ) %>%
  select(anio, distrito_txt, barrio_txt, poblacion_total_barrio, pob_25_39_barrio, pct_pob_25_39)
```

#### Join by normalized name

This source does not carry a neighbourhood code, only uppercase text with separators different from those of `barrios_madrid` (e.g. `"FUENCARRAL - EL PARDO"` vs `"Fuencarral-El Pardo"`), so the join is done by name, normalizing this table and `barrios_madrid`.

```{r union 6}
# stringi is already installed as a stringr dependency (part of tidyverse)
# defines a name-normalization function

normalizar_nombre <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") %>% # removes accents/diaeresis/ñ -> n
    str_to_upper() %>% # converts everything to uppercase
    str_replace_all("[^A-Z0-9]+", " ") %>% # any character (or run of one or more) that is ^ NOT an uppercase letter (A-Z) nor a digit (0-9) is replaced with a space " ".
    str_squish() # cleans up leftover leading/trailing or duplicate spaces just in case
}

# Applies the normalization function to barrios_madrid, creating two new columns (distrito_key, barrio_key) with the normalized versions of the names
barrios_madrid_norm <- barrios_madrid %>%
  mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(distrito_nombre),
         barrio_key = normalizar_nombre(barrio_nombre))

# Applies the same normalization to tramo_edad_ancho, and joins both tables using the normalized columns (distrito_key, barrio_key) as the key
tramo_edad_join <- tramo_edad_ancho %>%
  mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(distrito_txt),
         barrio_key = normalizar_nombre(barrio_txt)) %>%
  left_join(
    barrios_madrid_norm %>%
      select(distrito_key, barrio_key, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
    by = c("distrito_key", "barrio_key")
  )

# Final table: selects the final columns (dropping the original text columns and the normalization keys) and sorts
tramo_edad_barrio_anio <- tramo_edad_join %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,
         poblacion_total_barrio, pob_25_39_barrio, pct_pob_25_39) %>% 
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

#### Correction of total population for 3 neighbourhoods

The 2018 data is unreliable for Casco Histórico de Vicálvaro, Valdebernardo and Valderrivas, since poblacion_total_barrio shows extreme values that year (69,994, 7 and 6 respectively). Therefore, these values will be replaced with the 2018 total population figures found in the 2019 edition of the indicator panel. Valdebernardo has no data for the "30 - 34" row nor "35 - 39", while Valderrivas has no data for the "30 - 34" row and Casco Histórico has a figure (possibly) calculated over the 69,994 total. For this reason, and since there is no reliable basis to compute the actual 2018 breakdown, these will be set to NA.

```{r}
# identifies the rows generating NAs
tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(is.na(pct_pob_25_39)) %>%
  select(anio, barrio_nombre, poblacion_total_barrio, pob_25_39_barrio, pct_pob_25_39)

# a breakdown problem, not a magnitude problem
tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(distrito_num == 19) %>%
  group_by(anio) %>%
  summarise(poblacion_total_distrito = sum(poblacion_total_barrio), .groups = "drop")

# tribble detailing the actual population values for 2018
poblacion_2018_vicalvaro_real <- tribble(
  ~codigo_barrio, ~poblacion_total_barrio_real,
  "191", 34200, # Casco Histórico de Vicálvaro
  "192", 17637, # Valdebernardo
  "193", 18180  # Valderrivas
) # values from panel_indicadores, 2019 edition (actual year 2018), row "Sexo de la población"

barrios_afectados_2018_vicalvaro <- poblacion_2018_vicalvaro_real$codigo_barrio

tramo_edad_barrio_anio <- tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  left_join(poblacion_2018_vicalvaro_real, by = "codigo_barrio") %>%
  mutate(
    corregir_esta_fila = anio == 2018 & codigo_barrio %in% barrios_afectados_2018_vicalvaro,
    poblacion_total_barrio = if_else(corregir_esta_fila, poblacion_total_barrio_real, poblacion_total_barrio), #  if the row is 2018 and is one of the affected neighbourhoods, the neighbourhood's actual total population is substituted.
    pob_25_39_barrio = if_else(corregir_esta_fila, NA_real_, pob_25_39_barrio), # renamed 
    pct_pob_25_39 = if_else(corregir_esta_fila, NA_real_, pct_pob_25_39) 
  ) %>%
  select(-poblacion_total_barrio_real, -corregir_esta_fila)

# check
tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(anio == 2018, codigo_barrio %in% barrios_afectados_2018_vicalvaro) %>%
  select(codigo_barrio, barrio_nombre, poblacion_total_barrio, pob_25_39_barrio, pct_pob_25_39)
```

```{r compro 6 sí}
stopifnot(all(tramo_edad_barrio_anio$pct_pob_25_39 >= 0 & tramo_edad_barrio_anio$pct_pob_25_39 < 1, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## Source 7: housing transactions (`transacciones_vivienda.csv`)

**Dataset comments**:

The variable extracted is rate of housing transactions per inehabitant in each neighbourhood. This dataset is at neighbourhood level and in long format. Coverage rate (source limitation): the file's footer states that the Colegio de Registradores captures between 95.3% (2020) and 98.4% (2019) of the actual transactions each year.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 7, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
transacciones_raw <- read_delim("../data/raw/transacciones_vivienda.csv", delim = ";", 
                          locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
                          skip = 5, col_names = TRUE, show_col_types = FALSE, # header after skipping 5 rows
                          col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>% # forces text: otherwise "." is read as decimal
  rename(anio_txt = ...1, distrito_txt = ...2, barrio_txt = ...3, transacciones_txt = Total) # renaming 4 columns


transacciones_datos <- transacciones_raw %>%
  filter(str_detect(anio_txt, "^\\d{4}$")) %>% # keeps only the rows where anio_txt is 4 digits
  filter(as.integer(anio_txt) <= 2023) %>% # discards years after 2023
  filter(barrio_txt != distrito_txt) %>% # discards the rows where the neighbourhood text is identical to the district text -> discards "Ciudad de Madrid" and district-total.
  filter(str_detect(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}\\.\\s")) # only real neighbourhoods with the "3 digits + period + space" pattern (discards "00. No consta")


parse_transacciones <- function(x) {
  x <- if_else(x == "..", NA_character_, x) # replaces the statistical-confidentiality sentinel with NA
  as.numeric(str_remove_all(x, "\\.")) # removes the thousands-separator trap
}


# Creates the final table with year, neighbourhood code, housing transactions and its rate
transacciones_vivienda_barrio_anio <- transacciones_datos %>%
  transmute(
    anio = as.integer(anio_txt),
    codigo_barrio = str_extract(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}"), # codigo_barrio extracted from the first 3 digits
    transacciones_vivienda_barrio = parse_transacciones(transacciones_txt) # builds the final columns (cleaning the originals with parse_transacciones)
  ) %>%
  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio),
            by = "codigo_barrio") %>% # joins this table with barrios_madrid, bringing in the rest of the neighbourhood information, matching on codigo_barrio (already created)


  # the transaction rate is added so it is comparable across neighbourhoods of different sizes
  left_join(tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio, poblacion_total_barrio),
            by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%
  mutate(tasa_transacciones_vivienda = transacciones_vivienda_barrio / poblacion_total_barrio) %>% # computes the rate
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,
         transacciones_vivienda_barrio, tasa_transacciones_vivienda) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

## Source 8: indicator panel (`panel_indicadores/`)

**Dataset comments**:

From this source 13 indicators are extracted (2017-2023, neighbourhood level): Density, Total population, Average household size, Single-parent households (woman/man, separately), Total number of households, Aging ratio, Over-aging ratio, Proportion of migrant people, People with Spanish/foreign nationality (count and %) and Higher-education level (count and %).

### Dataset cleaning

#### Reading per year and locating the data range

```{r lectura 81}
# To be able to read any edition of the indicator panel
# Open editions from 2017 to 2024 and iterate over 21 sheets

distritos_hojas_panel <- c("CENTRO", "ARGANZUELA", "RETIRO", "SALAMANCA", "CHAMARTÍN", "TETUÁN", "CHAMBERÍ",
  "FUENCARRAL-EL PARDO", "MONCLOA-ARAVACA", "LATINA", "CARABANCHEL", "USERA", "PUENTE DE VALLECAS",
  "MORATALAZ", "CIUDAD LINEAL", "HORTALEZA", "VILLAVERDE", "VILLA DE VALLECAS", "VICÁLVARO",
  "SAN BLAS-CANILLEJAS", "BARAJAS") # the 21 district sheet names, identical across every edition

archivo_edicion_panel <- function(anio_edicion) {
  archivo <- list.files("../data/raw/panel_indicadores",
                         pattern = paste0("^", anio_edicion, "_panel_indicadores\\.xlsx?$"),
                         full.names = TRUE) # .xls in 2017-2020, .xlsx from 2021 onward. # Looks within the folder for the file whose name exactly matches the pattern.
  stopifnot(length(archivo) == 1) # warns if more than one file matches that pattern, or none
  archivo
}

# Locating the data range with localizar_columnas_panel
# looks at the first rows and columns of the sheet searching for the word "Superficie" (which tells it which column holds the indicator labels) and the word "CIUDAD" (which tells it which column the data block starts in and which row the header with neighbourhood names is on) -> this can't be done with fixed positions since it varies by edition

localizar_columnas_panel <- function(raw) {
  esquina <- as.matrix(raw[1:min(10, nrow(raw)), 1:min(6, ncol(raw))]) # esquina is a small matrix (at most 10 rows × 6 columns) with the raw content of that area of the sheet.
  texto <- apply(esquina, c(1, 2), function(v) if (is.na(v)) NA_character_ else str_squish(as.character(v))) # each cell (1,2) of esquina stays NA text if it is NA, and otherwise is converted to text/has its spaces cleaned.

  pos_ciudad <- which(texto == "CIUDAD", arr.ind = TRUE) # compares each cell of the texto matrix against "CIUDAD" and returns a logical matrix of the same size. With arr.ind = TRUE it returns those positions as (row, column) pairs.
  pos_label  <- which(matrix(str_starts(texto, "Superficie \\("), nrow = nrow(texto)), arr.ind = TRUE) # rebuilds the matrix shape to extract positions after searching for a string with str_starts(), which flattens the results into a vector.

  list( # Builds the output list with the three keys
    label_col   = if (nrow(pos_label)  > 0) pos_label[1, "col"]  else NA_integer_, # takes the column number of the first cell that started with "Superficie" else: if no match was found returns NA
    ciudad_col  = if (nrow(pos_ciudad) > 0) pos_ciudad[1, "col"] else NA_integer_, # takes the column number of the first cell that is "CIUDAD"
    fila_header = if (nrow(pos_ciudad) > 0) pos_ciudad[1, "row"] else NA_integer_ # takes the row number of the first cell that is "CIUDAD"
  )
}
```

#### Numeric parsing, column-pair extraction and row location

Both functions are defined to solve problem a and problem b:

a.  Within the same edition some district sheets store numbers as text in European format and others as native Excel numbers. Also, a single period is ambiguous on its own (e.g.: "1.114"), so it is resolved by knowing in advance whether the indicator is a count (thousands separator) or a rate/proportion (decimal), the type defined in specs_panel.

b.  Each geography (City/District/Neighbourhood) occupies a pair of contiguous columns, but what each of those two columns represents depends on the indicator. Depending on the mode (which reflects the indicator's statistical meaning, decided in advance, in specs_panel) it is decided how to extract it. Position rule common to all three modes: if only one column has content, that is the value that will be used, whether A or B, using the determined mode.

-   mode = "simple", type = "proporcion": the indicator can only be a rate. The value may be in A or in B depending on the edition, and whichever has content is used (priority B, then A). -\> Density, Average age, Household size, aging, over-aging, migrants, unemployment.

-   mode = "simple", type = "conteo": the indicator is indeed an actual count. It is normally in the 2nd column (B); the 1st (A), if it exists, is the % over the overall geography (not comparable across neighbourhoods) and is ignored without being read - unless B is empty, in which case it becomes the value to use. -\> Total population, Number of households, single-parent households.

-   mode = "dual": both columns are useful and are read independently. 1st (A) = % over the geography itself and 2nd (B) = absolute count. If one is missing, only that one is left NA, without affecting the other. -\> Spanish/foreign nationality, education level.

Risk accepted in this extraction logic: The pipeline decides that if both have content, the 2nd is the useful value and the 1st is discarded. This rule is based on an empirical check, both manual and through iterations with Claude Code, however there is a risk that in some specific case the values are reversed.

```{r ayb 7}
# solution to problem a.
# type="proporcion": a period (without a comma) is a decimal and is not removed.
# type="conteo": a period followed by groups of exactly 3 digits IS a thousands separator and IS removed.

parse_num_panel <- function(x, tipo = c("conteo", "proporcion")) { # the types can be conteo or proporcion
  tipo <- match.arg(tipo) # match.arg() checks that tipo is one of those two

  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.numeric(x)) # if the cell already came as a native Excel number, it stays as is
  x <- as.character(x) # if it wasn't numeric it is converted to text
  if (is.na(x) || x == "") return(NA_real_) # and if it is empty or NA it becomes NA_real_


  # CASE 1: if the text contains a comma it is assumed to be European notation and then...
  if (str_detect(x, ",")) {
    x <- str_remove_all(x, "\\.") # all periods are removed from the text (they are thousands separators)
    x <- str_replace(x, ",", ".") # replaces the comma with a period
    return(as.numeric(x)) # and converts to number
  }

  # CASE 2: if there's no comma but there is a period, it depends on the indicator's type
  if (tipo == "conteo" && str_detect(x, "^\\d{1,3}(\\.\\d{3})+$")) { # when the indicator's type is conteo AND the pattern matches groups of three digits separated by a period.
    return(as.numeric(str_remove_all(x, "\\."))) # the periods are removed from the text (they are thousands separators)
  }

  # CASE 3: if the type is "proporcion" + if it is text in normal format (123) + a count that doesn't match the three-digit pattern.
  as.numeric(x)
}


# solution to problem b.
valor_par_panel <- function(raw, fila, col_inicio, modo = c("simple", "dual"), tipo = NULL) {
  # col.inicio is the column where the A-B pair starts
  # fila is where the indicator is located (already found with localizar_fila_panel)
  modo <- match.arg(modo)

  # reads the two values of the A-B pair and with a_ok and b_ok recreates a boolean flag, indicating whether cell a and cell b have real content.
  a <- raw[[fila, col_inicio]]
  b <- raw[[fila, col_inicio + 1]]
  a_ok <- !is.na(a) && a != ""
  b_ok <- !is.na(b) && b != ""

  # CASE 1, simple: if it has content B is used, if that one is empty A will be used. The earlier parse is used.
  if (modo == "simple") {
    if (b_ok) return(list(valor = parse_num_panel(b, tipo)))
    if (a_ok) return(list(valor = parse_num_panel(a, tipo)))
    return(list(valor = NA_real_))
  }

  # CASE 2, dual: A and B are read completely independently
  list(
    proporcion = if (a_ok) parse_num_panel(a, "proporcion") else NA_real_,
    valor = if (b_ok) parse_num_panel(b, "conteo") else NA_real_
  )
}


# Locating the panel's rows, the indicators

localizar_fila_panel <- function(raw, label_col, patron, excluir = NULL) {
  etiquetas <- raw[[label_col]] # extracts the whole indicator-label column from raw
  etiquetas_sq <- ifelse(!is.na(etiquetas), str_squish(as.character(etiquetas)), NA_character_) # if there is a value it converts it to text and applies space cleanup, otherwise NA.

  match_incluir <- str_detect(etiquetas_sq, regex(patron, ignore_case = TRUE)) # returns a TRUE/FALSE vector indicating which labels to include if they match the pattern (anywhere in their text, case-insensitively).
  match_incluir[is.na(match_incluir)] <- FALSE # sets FALSE in the previous vector wherever it is NA.

  if (!is.null(excluir)) { # in case there is an exclusion pattern (same logic)
    match_excluir <- str_detect(etiquetas_sq, regex(excluir, ignore_case = TRUE))
    match_excluir[is.na(match_excluir)] <- FALSE

    match_incluir <- match_incluir & !match_excluir # labels matching the sought pattern AND not matching the discard pattern are included.
  }
  which(match_incluir) # returns the positional indices where the vector is TRUE.
}
```

#### Neighbourhood-name aliases specific to this source

In this source, name normalization (as done in Source 6) is not enough to get a complete set of matches. These mismatch cases exist:

-   *Article added by the panel*: "Las Acacias"/"La Chopera"/"Las Delicias"/"La Estrella"/"Del Pilar"/"Las Águilas"/"Los Ángeles". Resolved by removing a leading article ("El/La/Los/Las/Del") as a second pass (it cannot be applied to all neighbourhoods in a first pass because it would first need to check whether there is already a match).

-   *Abbreviation*: "Villaverde Alto, C.H. Villaverde" vs "Villaverde Alto, Casco Histórico de Villaverde".

-   *Historical pre-2017-reorganization name* (2017 edition only): "San Andrés" (former name of "Villaverde Alto, Casco Histórico de Villaverde") and "Ambroz" (former name of "Valdebernardo", in Vicálvaro, before the mid-2017 restructuring of Vicálvaro's neighbourhoods) and "Palos de Moguer" (former name of "Palos de la Frontera", in Arganzuela), which also appears in editions after 2017, so it is treated as an alias in every edition, not just 2017.

```{r alias}
# tribble defining the neighbourhood aliases
alias_barrio_panel <- tribble(
  ~distrito_key, ~barrio_key_origen, ~barrio_key_canonico,
  "VICALVARO", "AMBROZ", "VALDEBERNARDO",
  "VILLAVERDE", "SAN ANDRES", "VILLAVERDE ALTO CASCO HISTORICO DE VILLAVERDE",
  "ARGANZUELA", "PALOS DE MOGUER", "PALOS DE LA FRONTERA"
)

# normalizes the indicator panel's names
normalizar_barrio_panel <- function(distrito_key, barrio_key) {
  b <- str_replace_all(barrio_key, "\\bC H\\b", "CASCO HISTORICO DE") # expands the abbreviation (CH as its own token, not as part of a word).
  b <- str_remove(b, "^(EL|LA|LOS|LAS|DEL) ") # removes the leading article ->

  # checks whether the district+neighbourhood combination matches any of the table's three historical aliases
  alias <- alias_barrio_panel$barrio_key_canonico[
    match(paste(distrito_key, barrio_key), paste(alias_barrio_panel$distrito_key, alias_barrio_panel$barrio_key_origen))]
  coalesce(alias, b) # if alias has a value that one is used; otherwise b is used.
}

# normalizes barrios_madrid_norm's names
# necessary so that removing the article doesn't break the join in districts where the canonical name DOES carry an article.
barrios_madrid_norm_panel <- barrios_madrid_norm %>%
  mutate(barrio_key = normalizar_barrio_panel(distrito_key, barrio_key))
```

Checked against 2017: every panel row finds a match, only the 3 neighbourhoods that did not yet exist (Ensanche de Vallecas, Valderrivas, El Cañaveral) are left unpaired on the canonical side.

#### Real year of each indicator, per edition

No single edition works for every indicator equally, so there are three families with different lag (this has been checked manually and with Claude Code):

```{r año real}
# This block builds three lookups that translate "actual year I want" -> "edition number where the data is found"

anio_edicion_poblacion <- list("2017" = 2017, "2018" = 2019, "2019" = 2020, "2021" = 2021, "2022" = 2022, "2023" = 2023)
# no panel edition carries 2020 population/density -> substituted with tramo_edad/ further below.

anio_edicion_hogares <- list("2017" = 2017, "2018" = 2019, "2019" = 2020, "2020" = 2021, "2021" = 2022, "2022" = 2023, "2023" = 2024)
# household size, single-parent households, number of households, aging, over-aging, migrants, nationalities, education level.

ediciones_necesarias <- sort(unique(unlist(c(anio_edicion_poblacion, anio_edicion_hogares))))

ediciones_necesarias # 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 -> the 2018 one is never needed since it only provides 2016 data.
```

#### Reading the indicator panel editions

```{r lectura 82}
# processes ONE indicator (one panel row) and returns the column(s) that correspond to it
# locates the row, checks that it is unique, extracts the value for each neighbourhood creating one column ("simple" mode) or two ("dual" mode)

procesar_indicador <- function(raw, cols, barrio_cols, nombre_col, spec, anio_edicion, hoja) {
  fila_ind <- localizar_fila_panel(raw, cols$label_col, spec$patron, spec$excluir) # looks up this indicator's row, using the inclusion pattern and the exclusion pattern.

  # checks that exactly one row was found, otherwise stops execution
  if (length(fila_ind) != 1) {
    stop(sprintf("Edition %d, sheet %s, indicator %s: %d rows found (1 expected)",
                  anio_edicion, hoja, nombre_col, length(fila_ind)))
  }

  # for each neighbourhood column extracts the value with valor_par_panel() using modo and tipo
  valores <- map(barrio_cols, ~ valor_par_panel(raw, fila_ind, .x, modo = spec$modo, tipo = spec$tipo))

  # Depending on the mode, generates the function's result: columnas (the variable names) and valores paired by position.
  if (spec$modo == "dual") {
    list(
      columnas = c(paste0(nombre_col, "_pct"), nombre_col),
      valores = list(map_dbl(valores, "proporcion"), map_dbl(valores, "valor")))
  } else {
    list(columnas = nombre_col, valores = list(map_dbl(valores, "valor")))
  }
}


# function that reads one full panel edition (21 sheets) and extracts the indicators
leer_edicion_multiindicador <- function(anio_edicion, specs) {
  archivo <- archivo_edicion_panel(anio_edicion)
  map_dfr(distritos_hojas_panel, function(hoja) { # applies the function and combines all results into a single data frame by stacking rows

    raw <- read_excel(archivo, sheet = hoja, col_names = FALSE) # reads the sheet without a header
    cols <- localizar_columnas_panel(raw) # applies localizar_columnas_panel (data range)
    barrio_cols_all <- seq(cols$ciudad_col + 4, ncol(raw), by = 2) # Computes the columns where each neighbourhood's pair starts, generating a sequence skipping two at a time, because each geography occupies 2 columns. Skips the first 4 columns from the first CIUDAD column, which correspond to the 4 columns of CIUDAD + Distrito (checked manually).

    # for each value of barrio_cols_all extracts the header text: the neighbourhood name
    barrio_nombres_all <- map_chr(barrio_cols_all, ~ {
      v <- raw[[cols$fila_header, .x]]
      if (is.character(v) && !is.na(v)) str_squish(v) else NA_character_ # if there is text it cleans it, otherwise NA
    })

    # Filters the columns that did have a real neighbourhood name. barrio_cols and barrio_nombres end up as the "real column-real name" pairs.
    ok <- !is.na(barrio_nombres_all) & barrio_nombres_all != ""
    barrio_cols <- barrio_cols_all[ok]
    barrio_nombres <- barrio_nombres_all[ok]



    resultado <- tibble(distrito_txt = hoja, barrio_txt = barrio_nombres)
    # for each indicator in specs, it is processed (locate row + extract values) and
    # its resulting columns are added to `resultado` -- the detail of how each
    # indicator is processed lives in procesar_indicador(), defined above
    for (nombre_col in names(specs)) {
      r <- procesar_indicador(raw, cols, barrio_cols, nombre_col, specs[[nombre_col]], anio_edicion, hoja)
      for (i in seq_along(r$columnas)) resultado[[r$columnas[i]]] <- r$valores[[i]] # takes the columns (new variables) and values and adds them to the results table
    }
    resultado
  })
}
```

Cases with text variants across editions, all confirmed against the actual files: - aging/over-aging: "Proporción de..." 2017-2023, "Porcentaje de..." 2024 - migrants (non-OECD/EU): "Proporción de inmigrantes..." 2017-2020, "...personas migrantes..." 2021-2024. - Spanish/foreign nationality: carry their own date in parentheses from 2021 onward, so the pattern optionally allows it. - Number of households: "Nº total de hogares" 2017-2023, "Total hogares" in 2024. - education level: due to various typographical errors the pattern is anchored on "no universitario", which is stable across all of them.

```{r patrones 8}
# Row patterns per indicator: details the pattern to identify its label text and the modo/tipo specifications.

specs_panel <- list(
  densidad = list(patron = "^Densidad \\(", modo = "simple", tipo = "proporcion"),

  poblacion_total_panel = list(patron = "^Sexo de la población$", modo = "simple", tipo = "conteo"),

  tamano_hogar = list(patron = "^Tamaño medio del hogar", modo = "simple", tipo = "proporcion"),

  monop_mujer = list(patron = "^Hogares monoparentales: una mujer adulta", modo = "simple", tipo = "conteo"),

  monop_hombre = list(patron = "^Hogares monoparentales: un hombre adulto", modo = "simple", tipo = "conteo"),

  n_hogares = list(patron = "^(Nº total de hogares|Total hogares)$", modo = "simple", tipo = "conteo"),

  envejecimiento = list(patron = "^(Proporción|Porcentaje) de envejecimiento", modo = "simple", tipo = "proporcion"),

  sobreenvejecimiento = list(patron = "^(Proporción|Porcentaje) de sobre-?envejecimiento", modo = "simple", tipo = "proporcion"),

  migrantes = list(patron = "^Proporción de (inmigrantes|personas migrantes)", modo = "simple", tipo = "proporcion"),

  nac_espanola = list(patron = "^Personas con nacionalidad española(\\s*\\(.*\\))?$", modo = "dual"),

  nac_extranjera = list(patron = "^Personas con nacionalidad extranjera(\\s*\\(.*\\))?$", modo = "dual"),

  nivel_estudios_superiores = list(patron = "estudios superior.*no universitario|no universitario.*estudios superior", modo = "dual")
)

# Only the "hogares" family (see the actual-year tables further below) needs the 2024 edition
specs_panel_familia_hogares <- specs_panel[c("tamano_hogar", "monop_mujer", "monop_hombre", "n_hogares",
  "envejecimiento", "sobreenvejecimiento", "migrantes", "nac_espanola", "nac_extranjera", "nivel_estudios_superiores")]
```

```{r lectura 83, message=FALSE}
# This function takes one full edition already read with leer_edicion_multiindicador() and turns it into a table with codigo_barrio.

leer_edicion_normalizada <- function(anio_edicion, specs) {
  tabla <- leer_edicion_multiindicador(anio_edicion, specs) # calls the previous function building that edition's full table.

  tabla_join <- tabla %>%
    mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(distrito_txt), barrio_key = normalizar_nombre(barrio_txt)) %>% # creates distrito_key and barrio_key columns by applying normalizar_nombre (created in source 6)

    mutate(barrio_key = normalizar_barrio_panel(distrito_key, barrio_key)) %>% # changes barrio_key by applying the normalizar_barrio_panel function defined earlier.

    left_join(
      barrios_madrid_norm_panel %>%
        select(distrito_key, barrio_key, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio), by = c("distrito_key", "barrio_key")) # joins the table with barrios_madrid_norm_panel -> with already-normalized neighbourhood names.


  n_sin_barrio <- sum(is.na(tabla_join$codigo_barrio)) # counts how many rows of tabla_join were left without codigo_barrio
  if (n_sin_barrio > 0) { # if there is at least one unmatched row, locate where
    stop(sprintf("Edition %d: %d rows without a neighbourhood after normalizing (%s does not cover all cases)", anio_edicion, n_sin_barrio, "normalizar_barrio_panel()"))
  }
  tabla_join %>% select(-distrito_txt, -barrio_txt, -distrito_key, -barrio_key)
}

# reads each of the necessary editions (keeps the editions separate in a list).
datos_por_edicion_panel <- map(ediciones_necesarias, function(ed) {
  specs_usar <- if (ed == 2024) specs_panel_familia_hogares else specs_panel # only the 2024 edition is used exclusively for the "hogares" family, for the rest the specs_panel indicators are looked up
  leer_edicion_normalizada(ed, specs_usar) # reads the edition and normalizes it to codigo_barrio (function above)
})

# replaces the names of datos_por_edicion_panel with what's on the right-hand side ("2017-2024")
names(datos_por_edicion_panel) <- as.character(ediciones_necesarias)
```

#### Assembly by actual year

```{r ensamblado 8}
# This function joins, for each actual year (2017 to 2023), the population columns and the household columns, taking them from whichever edition corresponds to each family.

claves_barrio_panel <- c("distrito_num", "distrito_nombre", "barrio_num", "barrio_nombre", "codigo_barrio") # full neighbourhood identification

# variables belonging to each family (in terms of edition lag)
cols_poblacion <- c("densidad", "poblacion_total_panel")
cols_hogares <- c("tamano_hogar", "monop_mujer", "monop_hombre", "n_hogares",
  "envejecimiento", "sobreenvejecimiento", "migrantes",
  "nac_espanola_pct", "nac_espanola", "nac_extranjera_pct", "nac_extranjera",
  "nivel_estudios_superiores_pct", "nivel_estudios_superiores")

# Joined on the already-normalized codigo_barrio (and the rest of the keys).
ensamblar_anio_real <- function(anio_real) {
  base <- NULL

  ed_pob <- anio_edicion_poblacion[[as.character(anio_real)]] # looks up in the anio_edicion_poblacion table which edition carries the population data for this actual year (if there is no entry, as in 2020, it returns NULL).

  if (!is.null(ed_pob)) { # if it is not NULL... selects the relevant columns
    tabla <- datos_por_edicion_panel[[as.character(ed_pob)]] %>% select(all_of(claves_barrio_panel), all_of(cols_poblacion))
    base <- tabla
  }

  ed_hog <- anio_edicion_hogares[[as.character(anio_real)]] # same logic for the other family
  if (!is.null(ed_hog)) {
    tabla <- datos_por_edicion_panel[[as.character(ed_hog)]] %>% # looks up in the anio_edicion_hogares table which edition carries the population data for this actual year
    select(all_of(claves_barrio_panel), all_of(cols_hogares))
    base <- if (is.null(base)) tabla else full_join(base, tabla, by = claves_barrio_panel)
  }

  base %>% mutate(anio = anio_real, .before = 1) # adds an actual-year column
}
panel_largo <- map_dfr(2017:2023, ensamblar_anio_real) # combines the data with actual years into a single table
```

#### Correction of density and total population variables in 2020

No panel edition carries 2020 population and density, but both figures could be extracted from `tramo_edad_barrio_anio` (Source 6). Density is recomputed with that population divided by the neighbourhood's Surface area (since it is a stable value, 2020 will be used).

```{r sustitucion 8, message=FALSE}
# reuses leer_edicion_normalizada() but with a specs list for the "Superficie" indicator.
leer_superficie_barrio <- function(anio_edicion) {
  leer_edicion_normalizada(anio_edicion, list(
    superficie_ha = list(patron = "^Superficie \\(", modo = "simple", tipo = "proporcion")
  ))
}
superficie_barrio_panel <- leer_superficie_barrio(2020)


sustituto_2020 <- tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(anio == 2020) %>% # Filters only 2020 from Source 6's table
  select(codigo_barrio, poblacion_total_barrio) %>%
  left_join(superficie_barrio_panel %>% select(codigo_barrio, superficie_ha), by = "codigo_barrio") # joins the surface area to that table, matching on codigo_barrio


# checks that no neighbourhood was left without a surface area after the join
stopifnot(sum(is.na(sustituto_2020$superficie_ha)) == 0) # if this fails, 2023 works.

# the result is left with just codigo_barrio, the renamed population, and the computed density.
sustituto_2020 <- sustituto_2020 %>%
  transmute(
    codigo_barrio,
    poblacion_total_panel_sust = poblacion_total_barrio,
    densidad_sust = poblacion_total_barrio / superficie_ha)

# Actual substitution of the density and population variables in 2020
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio  <- panel_largo %>%
  left_join(sustituto_2020, by = "codigo_barrio") %>% # joins the substitute to the panel (with actual year)
  mutate(
    poblacion_total_panel = if_else(anio == 2020, poblacion_total_panel_sust, poblacion_total_panel), # replaces the variables in the rows where the actual year is 2020, and for the other years keeps the value it already had
    densidad = if_else(anio == 2020, densidad_sust, densidad)
  ) %>% select(-poblacion_total_panel_sust, -densidad_sust) # the already-used substitutes are dropped
```

#### Correction of nac_espanola_pct / nac_extranjera_pct

The percentage column for both Spanish and foreign nationality that the indicator panel source itself provides is not reliable, even producing percentages above 100% in some cases (Atocha 2021 = 104.5%, El Cañaveral 2021 = 162.2%). The error also appears in El Cañaveral and Atocha in 2020 and 2022, and in several more neighbourhoods only in 2022 (Ángeles, Quintana, Ventas, San Pascual). Since it has been verified that `nac_espanola + nac_extranjera` matches `poblacion_total_panel` with a median error margin of 0% (90th percentile value of 0, and an absolute maximum of 0.83%), the calculation of both percentages is validated from the count and `poblacion_total_panel`, instead of using the "%" that the source itself provides.

```{r}
# check for percentages > 1 (above 100% in the raw data) -> El Cañaveral and Atocha 2021
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(nac_espanola_pct > 1 | nac_extranjera_pct > 1) %>%
  select(anio, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, nac_espanola_pct, nac_extranjera_pct)

# pct_calculado is the one extracted from count/total population, while nac_espanola_pct is the % that appears as data in the indicator panel -> there is a difference in several cases.
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(
    pct_calculado = nac_espanola / poblacion_total_panel,
    diferencia = abs(nac_espanola_pct - pct_calculado)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(diferencia)) %>%
  select(anio, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, nac_espanola_pct, pct_calculado, diferencia,
         nac_espanola, nac_extranjera, poblacion_total_panel) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

# check nac_espanola + nac_extranjera = poblacion_total_panel
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(diferencia_relativa = (nac_espanola + nac_extranjera - poblacion_total_panel) / poblacion_total_panel) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    minimo = min(diferencia_relativa),
    mediana = median(diferencia_relativa),
    p90 = quantile(diferencia_relativa, 0.90), # at least 90% of the 914 rows have zero difference
    maximo = max(diferencia_relativa),
    max_absoluto = max(abs(diferencia_relativa)))
```

```{r correccion nacionalidad}
# substitution of the source's "%" with count/population
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio <- panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate( #  overwrites the two columns nac_espanola_pct and nac_extranjera_pct
    nac_espanola_pct = nac_espanola / poblacion_total_panel,
    nac_extranjera_pct = nac_extranjera / poblacion_total_panel)
```

#### Correction of the migrants variable in 2023

The `migrantes` variable (non-EU/rest-of-OECD foreigners) is by definition a subset of `nac_extranjera_pct` (all foreigners) and both are computed under the same population total. So, from the subtraction `nac_extranjera_pct - migrantes` one obtains those migrants originating from EU/OECD countries. In 2 neighbourhoods of Arganzuela in 2023 (Acacias, Legazpi) the subtraction is negative. This has been checked against the raw Excel of `2024_panel_indicadores.xlsx` (the edition that uses actual year 2023 for this indicator family), and it is observed that `migrantes` shows a jump in 2023 for both neighbourhoods compared to their previous years, while `nac_extranjera_pct` follows a smooth trend with no jump. The correction is limited to these 2 cases since the rest show data consistent with a genuine rise in the migrantes variable.

```{r correccion migrantes}
# identifies the neighbourhood-years where nac_extranjera_pct - migrantes comes out negative
filas_migrantes_no_fiable <- panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(diferencia_ue_ocde = nac_extranjera_pct - migrantes) %>% # subtraction
  filter(diferencia_ue_ocde < 0) %>%
  select(anio, codigo_barrio, barrio_nombre, nac_extranjera_pct, migrantes, diferencia_ue_ocde)
filas_migrantes_no_fiable

# checks that the "migrantes" problem is in Acacias and Legazpi 2023
stopifnot(nrow(filas_migrantes_no_fiable) == 2)
stopifnot(all(filas_migrantes_no_fiable$anio == 2023))
stopifnot(all(sort(filas_migrantes_no_fiable$codigo_barrio) == c("022", "024")))

# migrantes is set to NA only in the rows identified above
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio <- panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  left_join(filas_migrantes_no_fiable %>% transmute(anio, codigo_barrio, no_fiable = TRUE),
            by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%
  mutate(migrantes = if_else(!is.na(no_fiable), NA_real_, migrantes)) %>% # if it falls under unreliable it is set to NA, otherwise the same value is kept.
  select(-no_fiable)

# the subtraction is done -> creating the pct_extranjeros_ue_ocde variable
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio <- panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(pct_extranjeros_ue_ocde = nac_extranjera_pct - migrantes)
```

```{r tabla 8}
# Final table
panel_indicadores_barrio_anio <- panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,
         densidad, poblacion_total_panel,
         tamano_hogar, monop_mujer, monop_hombre, n_hogares,
         envejecimiento, sobreenvejecimiento, migrantes, pct_extranjeros_ue_ocde,
         nac_espanola_pct, nac_espanola, nac_extranjera_pct, nac_extranjera,
         nivel_estudios_superiores_pct, nivel_estudios_superiores) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

```{r compro 8}
# checks there is no neighbourhood left unjoined
stopifnot(sum(is.na(panel_largo$codigo_barrio)) == 0)

# checks the number of neighbourhoods per year
barrios_por_anio_panel <- panel_indicadores_barrio_anio %>% count(anio, name = "n_barrios")
stopifnot(barrios_por_anio_panel$n_barrios[barrios_por_anio_panel$anio == 2017] == 128)

stopifnot(sum(is.na(panel_indicadores_barrio_anio$pct_extranjeros_ue_ocde)) == 2)
```
