## Source 9: census of business premises (`censo_locales/`)

**Dataset comments**:

The following CNAE Divisions were chosen to build the variables, which deal only with "Abierto" (open) premises. There are two manual exclusions within 55 and 56, decided so those two groups are purer proxies of "tourism" and of "bars and restaurants". `559001` (Colegios Mayores and student halls of residence) is excluded from 55. `562901`-`562905` (canteens in sports facilities/offices, education centers, senior centers, social service centers, hospitals) are excluded from 56 since they are not restaurant establishments open to the public.

| Group | CNAE Divisions | Given name |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `comercio_menor` | 47 | Retail trade |
| `turismo_alojamiento` | 55 (minus `559001`) | Tourism and accommodation |
| `bares_restaurantes` | 56 (minus `562901`-`562905`) | Bars and restaurants |
| `inmobiliarias` | 68 | Real estate activities |
| `educacion` | 85 | Education |
| `sanitarias` | 86 | Health |
| `servicios_sociales` | 87 + 88 | Social services |
| `arte_recreo_ocio` | 90 + 91 + 93 | Arts, recreation and entertainment |

The variables extracted are the count and percentage of these establishment activities.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 9, warning=FALSE}
encoding_censo_por_anio <- c( # it has been confirmed that each file has a different encoding
  "2017" = "WINDOWS-1252", "2018" = "UTF-8", "2019" = "WINDOWS-1252",
  "2020" = "WINDOWS-1252", "2021" = "WINDOWS-1252", "2022" = "UTF-8", "2023" = "UTF-8"
)

# `id_barrio_local` is not `codigo_barrio`, so codigo_barrio is reconstructed (format "DDB", e.g. "083") from id_barrio_local (format district without a leading zero + 2-digit neighbourhood, e.g. "803")
id_barrio_local_a_codigo_barrio <- function(id_barrio_local) {
  id_num <- as.integer(id_barrio_local)
  distrito_num <- id_num %/% 100 # returns the district
  barrio_num <- id_num %% 100 # returns the neighbourhood
  sprintf("%02d%d", distrito_num, barrio_num) # rebuilds the codigo_barrio format
}

# function that reads the census of business premises
leer_censo_locales_raw_anio <- function(anio) {
  archivo <- sprintf("../data/raw/censo_locales/%d_locales.csv", anio)
  encoding <- encoding_censo_por_anio[[as.character(anio)]] # selects the encoding

# reads the file applying the encoding and forcing every column to be read as text (to prevent id_epigrafe from being read as a number and losing digits).
  raw <- read_delim(archivo, delim = ";",
                     locale = locale(encoding = encoding),
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)

  raw %>%
    transmute(
      anio = anio,
      codigo_barrio = id_barrio_local_a_codigo_barrio(id_barrio_local), # applies the reconstruction
      desc_situacion_local,
      id_division = if_else(str_detect(id_division, "^COMERCIO AL POR MENOR"), "47", str_squish(id_division)), # fixes the single data-corruption case that falls within the 8 groups of interest
      id_epigrafe = str_squish(id_epigrafe))
}

# Applied for every year
censo_locales_raw_todos <- map_dfr(2017:2023, leer_censo_locales_raw_anio)

# censo_locales_todos is created by keeping only the open premises
censo_locales_todos <- censo_locales_raw_todos %>%
  filter(desc_situacion_local == "Abierto") %>%
  select(anio, codigo_barrio, id_division, id_epigrafe)

# looks at the neighbourhoods that have premises records in the table
barrios_presentes_todos <- censo_locales_raw_todos %>% distinct(anio, codigo_barrio)
```

#### Economic-activity groups and filtering

```{r econom 9}
# definition of the economic-activity groups by Division level
division_a_grupo_econom <- tribble(
  ~id_division, ~grupo_comercial,
  "47", "comercio_menor",
  "55", "turismo_alojamiento",
  "56", "bares_restaurantes",
  "68", "inmobiliarias",
  "85", "educacion",
  "86", "sanitarias",
  "87", "servicios_sociales",
  "88", "servicios_sociales",
  "90", "arte_recreo_ocio",
  "91", "arte_recreo_ocio",
  "93", "arte_recreo_ocio"
)
cols_grupo <- unique(division_a_grupo_econom$grupo_comercial) # the 8 final groups

# definition of the manual exclusions of divisions 55 and 56
epigrafes_excluidos_manual <- c(
  "559001",
  "562901", "562902", "562903", "562904", "562905")

# denominator: total active premises per neighbourhood-year, over ALL divisions (not just the chosen ones)
total_locales_barrio_anio <- censo_locales_todos %>%
  count(anio, codigo_barrio, name = "n_locales_activos_total")

# numerator: only the premises from the 8 chosen divisions/groups, removing exclusions
conteo_grupo_barrio_anio <- censo_locales_todos %>%
  filter(!(id_epigrafe %in% epigrafes_excluidos_manual)) %>% # excludes epigraphs
  inner_join(division_a_grupo_econom, by = "id_division") %>% # keeps the chosen ones
  count(anio, codigo_barrio, grupo_comercial, name = "n") %>% # counts premises per neighbourhood-year-group
  pivot_wider(names_from = grupo_comercial, values_from = n, names_prefix = "n_", values_fill = 0) # converts that long format to wide, creating one column per economic group.
```

#### Neighbourhood × year grid and assembly

A real neighbourhood with no registered premises that year (Valderrivas/El Cañaveral in 2018) would disappear without generating any row. Because of this, a template of which neighbourhoods exist in which year is built (exception of 2017 with 128 neighbourhoods), and the count is joined to it even if it is 0. In this case, the only neighbourhoods with no row at all in the raw data are Valderrivas and El Cañaveral (`barrios_sin_cobertura`) since they are neighbourhoods created recently in 2018, so it is possible that, whether due to economic activity not yet being located in that neighbourhood or due to it not yet being recorded in an emerging area, there is no data about it.

```{r grid 9}
barrios_sin_entidad_2017 <- c("183", "193", "194") # neighbourhoods that did not yet exist in 2017

# removes those neighbourhoods only when the year is 2017, the rest stays the same.
grid_censo_barrio_anio <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio) {
  base <- barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio)
  if (anio == 2017) base <- base %>% filter(!codigo_barrio %in% barrios_sin_entidad_2017)
  base %>% mutate(anio = anio, .before = 1)
})

# computes the neighbourhoods without coverage
barrios_sin_cobertura <- grid_censo_barrio_anio %>%
  select(anio, codigo_barrio) %>%
  anti_join(barrios_presentes_todos, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio"))


# Final assembly
censo_locales_barrio_anio <- grid_censo_barrio_anio %>%
  left_join(total_locales_barrio_anio, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%

  left_join(barrios_sin_cobertura %>% mutate(sin_cobertura = TRUE), by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%
  mutate(
    sin_cobertura = replace_na(sin_cobertura, FALSE),
    n_locales_activos_total = case_when(
      !is.na(n_locales_activos_total) ~ n_locales_activos_total, # active = at least 1 open premise
      sin_cobertura              ~ 0, 
      TRUE                       ~ 0 # 0 rows in the raw data
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Same pattern for the 8 per-group columns
  left_join(conteo_grupo_barrio_anio, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(paste0("n_", cols_grupo)),
                ~ case_when(
                    is.na(n_locales_activos_total) ~ NA_real_,
                    n_locales_activos_total == 0    ~ 0,
                    TRUE                             ~ replace_na(.x, 0)
                ))) %>%

  mutate(across(all_of(paste0("n_", cols_grupo)),
                ~ case_when(
                    sin_cobertura                 ~ 0, 
                    n_locales_activos_total == 0  ~ NA_real_, 
                    TRUE                           ~ .x / n_locales_activos_total
                ),
                .names = "pct_{sub('^n_', '', .col)}")) %>% # if sin_cobertura, the result is 0; if n_locales_activos_total is 0 for another reason, the result is NA (undefined, 0/0); otherwise, computes the group's share of total active premises.
  select(-sin_cobertura) %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,
         all_of(paste0("n_", cols_grupo)), all_of(paste0("pct_", cols_grupo)),
         n_locales_activos_total) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

#### Premises in residential use

```{r uso vivienda 9}
# % of premises in residential use
total_locales_todos_estados <- censo_locales_raw_todos %>%
  count(anio, codigo_barrio, name = "n_locales_todos_estados") # counts every kind of premise

conteo_uso_vivienda <- censo_locales_raw_todos %>%
  filter(desc_situacion_local == "Uso vivienda") %>%
  count(anio, codigo_barrio, name = "n_uso_vivienda") # counts the premises used as housing

# Same logic as the previous case
uso_vivienda_barrio_anio <- grid_censo_barrio_anio %>%
  left_join(total_locales_todos_estados, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>% # adds n_locales_todos_estados
  left_join(conteo_uso_vivienda, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>% # adds n_uso_vivienda
  left_join(barrios_sin_cobertura %>% mutate(sin_cobertura = TRUE), by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>% # flag for cases with or without coverage
  
  mutate(
    sin_cobertura = replace_na(sin_cobertura, FALSE),
    n_locales_todos_estados = case_when(
      !is.na(n_locales_todos_estados) ~ n_locales_todos_estados,
      sin_cobertura ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    n_uso_vivienda = case_when(
      is.na(n_locales_todos_estados) ~ NA_real_,
      n_locales_todos_estados == 0    ~ 0,
      TRUE                             ~ replace_na(n_uso_vivienda, 0)
    ),
    # computes the percentage of establishments used as housing for every case that doesn't have a 0 denominator, except sin_cobertura, which is 0
    pct_uso_vivienda = case_when(
      sin_cobertura                 ~ 0, 
      n_locales_todos_estados == 0  ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE                           ~ n_uso_vivienda / n_locales_todos_estados
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-sin_cobertura) %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,
         n_locales_todos_estados, n_uso_vivienda, pct_uso_vivienda) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)



# join with the main table
censo_locales_barrio_anio <- censo_locales_barrio_anio %>%
  left_join(
    uso_vivienda_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio, n_locales_todos_estados, n_uso_vivienda, pct_uso_vivienda), by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio"))
```

```{r compro 9}
stopifnot(all(censo_locales_raw_todos$codigo_barrio %in% barrios_madrid$codigo_barrio))

# checks that the 8 economic groups appear as a column (none is left completely empty)
stopifnot(all(paste0("n_", cols_grupo) %in% names(conteo_grupo_barrio_anio)))

# checks that no neighbourhood is left unjoined

stopifnot(conteo_barrios_censo$n[conteo_barrios_censo$anio == 2017] == 128)
stopifnot(all(conteo_barrios_censo$n[conteo_barrios_censo$anio != 2017] == 131))

stopifnot(all(sapply(censo_locales_barrio_anio[pct_cols], function(x) all(x >= 0 & x <= 1, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

## Source 10: residential churn (`churn_total/`)

**Dataset comments**:

These variables are built from 4 Banco de Datos files that record Padrón registrations and deregistrations. They are proxies for population turnover, resident inflow and outflow rates per neighbourhood-year. They are computed keeping the direction of the movement but collapsing 2 origins, giving 1) domestic registrations (altas) / deregistrations (bajas), internal to the city of Madrid, 2) residential registrations/deregistrations, external to the city. Dividing by the neighbourhood's total population to compute the rates normalizes the absolute counts by population size, so they are comparable between large and small neighbourhoods.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 10}
parse_num_churn <- function(x) as.numeric(str_remove_all(x, "\\.")) # removes the thousands-separator period

leer_churn_archivo <- function(nombre_archivo) {
  archivo <- sprintf("../data/raw/churn_total/%s.xlsx", nombre_archivo)
  read_excel(archivo, sheet = 1, skip = 8, # sheet 1, skips 8 rows
             col_names = c("anio_txt", "distrito_txt", "barrio_txt", "total_txt", "espanola_txt", "extranjera_txt"), col_types = "text") %>% # forces them to be read as text
    filter(str_detect(anio_txt, "^\\d{4}$")) %>% # discards footer rows using the 4-digit year pattern

    filter(as.integer(anio_txt) <= 2023) %>% # filters years less than 2023
    filter(barrio_txt != distrito_txt) %>% # discards "Ciudad de Madrid" and the district-total rows by removing those rows that have the same text in both columns
    filter(str_detect(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}\\.\\s")) %>% # only real neighbourhoods (3-digit pattern)
    filter(!str_detect(barrio_txt, regex("No consta", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% # "000. No consta" does match the 3-digit pattern, so it is explicitly excluded

    transmute(
      anio = as.integer(anio_txt),
      codigo_barrio = str_extract(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}"), # neighbourhood code extraction
      total = parse_num_churn(total_txt),
      espanola = parse_num_churn(espanola_txt), # applies the parse
      extranjera = parse_num_churn(extranjera_txt))
}


# total/española/extranjera are renamed with the flow's prefix, so the 4 can be joined without column overlap
renombrar_flujo_churn <- function(df, prefijo) {
  df %>% rename_with(~ paste0(prefijo, "_", .x), c(total, espanola, extranjera))
} # function that defines how the renaming is done

altas_internas_churn <- leer_churn_archivo("altas_domicilio_interno") %>% renombrar_flujo_churn("altas_internas") # prefix set for each file according to direction and origin
bajas_internas_churn <- leer_churn_archivo("bajas_domicilio_interno") %>% renombrar_flujo_churn("bajas_internas")
altas_externas_churn <- leer_churn_archivo("altas_residencia_externo") %>% renombrar_flujo_churn("altas_externas")
bajas_externas_churn <- leer_churn_archivo("bajas_residencia_externo") %>% renombrar_flujo_churn("bajas_externas")
```

#### Joining the 4 flows, totals and rates

```{r union 10}
# the 4 tables are joined into one, matching on anio and codigo_barrio
churn_join <- altas_internas_churn %>%
  full_join(bajas_internas_churn, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%
  full_join(altas_externas_churn, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>%
  full_join(bajas_externas_churn, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio"))

# computes total inflows and outflows (origin is collapsed, direction is kept)
churn_totales <- churn_join %>%
  mutate(
    entradas_totales_total = altas_internas_total + altas_externas_total,
    salidas_totales_total = bajas_internas_total + bajas_externas_total
  )

# uses the neighbourhood population already built in Source 6 (age bracket)
poblacion_para_churn <- tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio, poblacion_total_barrio)

churn_con_poblacion <- churn_totales %>%
  left_join(poblacion_para_churn, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio")) %>% # adds each neighbourhood-year's population from source 6
  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio), by = "codigo_barrio") # adds barrios_madrid identifiers


# Computes 6 rates, dividing each flow and the totals by the neighbourhood-year population.
churn_total_barrio_anio <- churn_con_poblacion %>%
  mutate(
    tasa_altas_internas = altas_internas_total / poblacion_total_barrio,
    tasa_bajas_internas = bajas_internas_total / poblacion_total_barrio,
    tasa_altas_externas = altas_externas_total / poblacion_total_barrio,
    tasa_bajas_externas = bajas_externas_total / poblacion_total_barrio,
    tasa_entradas_totales = entradas_totales_total / poblacion_total_barrio,
    tasa_salidas_totales = salidas_totales_total / poblacion_total_barrio
  ) %>%

# the final columns are renamed
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,
         n_altas_internas = altas_internas_total, n_altas_internas_esp = altas_internas_espanola, n_altas_internas_ext = altas_internas_extranjera,
         n_bajas_internas = bajas_internas_total, n_bajas_internas_esp = bajas_internas_espanola, n_bajas_internas_ext = bajas_internas_extranjera,
         n_altas_externas = altas_externas_total, n_altas_externas_esp = altas_externas_espanola, n_altas_externas_ext = altas_externas_extranjera,
         n_bajas_externas = bajas_externas_total, n_bajas_externas_esp = bajas_externas_espanola, n_bajas_externas_ext = bajas_externas_extranjera,
         n_entradas_totales = entradas_totales_total, n_salidas_totales = salidas_totales_total,
         poblacion_total_barrio,
         tasa_altas_internas, tasa_bajas_internas, tasa_altas_externas, tasa_bajas_externas,
         tasa_entradas_totales, tasa_salidas_totales) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 10}
# checks the number of neighbourhoods in each year
stopifnot(all(count(churn_total_barrio_anio, anio)$n == 131))
stopifnot(sum(is.na(churn_total_barrio_anio$distrito_num)) == 0)

# checks that the rates are not negative
tasa_cols_churn <- c("tasa_altas_internas", "tasa_bajas_internas", "tasa_altas_externas",
                     "tasa_bajas_externas", "tasa_entradas_totales", "tasa_salidas_totales")
stopifnot(all(sapply(churn_total_barrio_anio[tasa_cols_churn], function(x) all(x >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))))

# checks the rows where the population left_join found no match: the expected ones are the 3 neighbourhoods of 2017 that tramo_edad/ does not cover.
barrios_sin_poblacion_churn <- churn_con_poblacion %>% filter(is.na(poblacion_total_barrio))
stopifnot(nrow(barrios_sin_poblacion_churn) == 3)
stopifnot(all(barrios_sin_poblacion_churn$anio == 2017))
stopifnot(all(sort(barrios_sin_poblacion_churn$codigo_barrio) == c("183", "193", "194")))

# checks internal consistency: city-wide total altas_domicilio_interno = city-wide total bajas_domicilio_interno

# 1. In the raw file
altas_internas_ciudad <- read_excel("../data/raw/churn_total/altas_domicilio_interno.xlsx", sheet = 1, skip = 8, col_names = c("anio_txt", "distrito_txt", "barrio_txt", "total_txt", "espanola_txt", "extranjera_txt"), col_types = "text") %>% # re-reads the raw domicile-registrations file
  filter(distrito_txt == "Ciudad de Madrid") %>% # selects the Ciudad de Madrid total
  transmute(anio = as.integer(anio_txt), total = parse_num_churn(total_txt))

bajas_internas_ciudad <- read_excel("../data/raw/churn_total/bajas_domicilio_interno.xlsx", sheet = 1, skip = 8, col_names = c("anio_txt", "distrito_txt", "barrio_txt", "total_txt", "espanola_txt", "extranjera_txt"), col_types = "text") %>% # re-reads the raw domicile-deregistrations file
  filter(distrito_txt == "Ciudad de Madrid") %>% # selects the Ciudad de Madrid total
  transmute(anio = as.integer(anio_txt), total = parse_num_churn(total_txt))

stopifnot(nrow(altas_internas_ciudad) == 7, nrow(bajas_internas_ciudad) == 7) # checks that 7 rows were included, one per year
stopifnot(all(altas_internas_ciudad$total == bajas_internas_ciudad$total)) # checks that the Ciudad de Madrid registration and deregistration totals in the raw files are equal


# 2. In the processed file versus the raw file
# checks consistency between the raw file's city total and the sum of your already-processed neighbourhoods (verifies a sound cleaning pipeline)
suma_altas_internas_procesado <- churn_total_barrio_anio %>% # registrations
  group_by(anio) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n_altas_internas, na.rm = TRUE))

# known exception in 2023, the "Ciudad de Madrid" total in altas_domicilio_interno.xlsx does not match the sum of its own 21 districts (198349 vs 198342, a difference of -7) -> confirmed in the raw file
diferencia_altas <- suma_altas_internas_procesado$total - altas_internas_ciudad$total
stopifnot(all(diferencia_altas == if_else(suma_altas_internas_procesado$anio == 2023, -7, 0)))

suma_bajas_internas_procesado <- churn_total_barrio_anio %>%
  group_by(anio) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n_bajas_internas, na.rm = TRUE))

# known exception in 2023, the "Ciudad de Madrid" total in bajas_domicilio_interno.xlsx does not match the sum of its own 21 districts (198349 vs 198003, a difference of -346) -> confirmed in the raw file
diferencia_bajas <- suma_bajas_internas_procesado$total - bajas_internas_ciudad$total
stopifnot(all(diferencia_bajas == if_else(suma_bajas_internas_procesado$anio == 2023, -346, 0)))
```

## Source 11: municipal investment by district (`inversiones_ayto_distritos.xlsx`)

**Dataset comments**:

The variables extracted are investment budget and actual spending by district and the intensity of investment based on the budget and actual spending. The intensity is understood as the value divided by the district population. Since this data it only exists at district level, so each neighbourhood inherits its district's value, without adding real variance at neighbourhood level. The denominator of the investment-intensity variable is the district's population, which makes it comparable across districts of different sizes. The only population gap is the one in tramo_edad/ in 2017.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 11}
# extracts the districts from barrios_madrid and applies the name normalization (defined earlier) to their names
distritos_norm_inv <- barrios_madrid %>%
  distinct(distrito_num, distrito_nombre) %>%
  mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(distrito_nombre))

inversiones_distrito_raw <- read_excel("../data/raw/inversiones_ayto_distritos.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet") %>%
  rename(anio = `Año`, id_area = `Id Área`, nombre_area = `Nombre Área`,
         presupuesto_gasto = `Presupuesto Gasto`, gasto_real = `Gasto Real`) %>%
  filter(anio >= 2017, anio <= 2023) %>% # filters to the study window
  filter(!id_area %in% c("NA", "NN")) %>% # discards "No distritalizable" and "Varios distritos"
  mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(nombre_area)) # normalizes the area = district name

inversiones_distrito <- inversiones_distrito_raw %>% # joins both tables
  left_join(distritos_norm_inv %>% select(distrito_key, distrito_num), by = "distrito_key")

```

#### District population and investment intensity

```{r tasas 11}
# reuses the table built in Source 6 that gives population per neighbourhood-year and aggregates it to district level
poblacion_distrito <- tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  group_by(anio, distrito_num) %>%
  summarise(poblacion_total_distrito = sum(poblacion_total_barrio), .groups = "drop")

inversiones_distrito_pob <- inversiones_distrito %>%
  left_join(poblacion_distrito, by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>% # adds the district's population to the previous table
  mutate( # computes the two rates
    intensidad_inversion_presupuesto = presupuesto_gasto / poblacion_total_distrito, # budget
    intensidad_inversion_real = gasto_real / poblacion_total_distrito) # actual spending
```

#### Broadcast to neighbourhood

```{r broadcast 11}
barrios_sin_entidad_2017_inv <- c("183", "193", "194") # 2017's missing neighbourhoods

# removes those neighbourhoods only when the year is 2017, the rest stays the same.
grid_barrio_anio_inv <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio) {
  base <- barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio)
  if (anio == 2017) base <- base %>% filter(!codigo_barrio %in% barrios_sin_entidad_2017_inv)
  base %>% mutate(anio = anio, .before = 1)
})

# broadcast: since several neighbourhoods share the same district, each one of them receives the same investment value from its district.
inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio <- grid_barrio_anio_inv %>%
  left_join(inversiones_distrito_pob %>%
              select(anio, distrito_num, # renamed with the _distrito suffix
                     presupuesto_gasto_distrito = presupuesto_gasto,
                     gasto_real_distrito = gasto_real,
                     poblacion_total_distrito,
                     intensidad_inversion_presupuesto_distrito = intensidad_inversion_presupuesto,
                     intensidad_inversion_real_distrito = intensidad_inversion_real),
            by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 11}
# checks that every district in both tables (distritos_norm_inv and inversiones_distrito_raw) found a match after the join
stopifnot(sum(is.na(inversiones_distrito$distrito_num)) == 0)

# checks that there are 21 neighbourhoods for each year in the resulting joined table
stopifnot(nrow(inversiones_distrito) == 21 * 7)

# checks that the broadcast left no neighbourhood without investment data (no NA)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio)) == 0)

# every neighbourhood within the same district-year must have exactly the same value (correct broadcast) -> n=1
chk_broadcast_inv <- inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio %>%
  group_by(anio, distrito_num) %>% # groups by year and district
  summarise(n_valores_distintos = n_distinct(presupuesto_gasto_distrito), .groups = "drop") # counts how many distinct values there are in each group
stopifnot(all(chk_broadcast_inv$n_valores_distintos == 1))
```

### Saving

```{r save 11}
write_csv(inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio, "../data/processed/inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio.csv")
```

### View of the final table

```{r view 11}
#| eval: false
inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio <- read_csv("../data/processed/inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
View(inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio)
```

## Source 12: municipal investment by district and category (`inversiones_tipo_distrito/`)

**Dataset comments**:

The variables extracted in this section are the amount of investment (divided in budget and actual spending) of each type and its share compared to the total amount of budget and actual spending. This is a district-level source that complements Source 11 with the breakdown by spending category (for now all investment categories are extracted, even though not all of them appear every year in every district). Rows that have an empty `Gasto Real` - a category with a budget assigned but with the budget execution not reported - are kept as NA.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 12}
# dictionary of names for the 15 investment categories
categorias_inversion <- tribble(
  ~id_linea, ~categoria,
  "X00", "caracter_general",
  "X01", "proteccion_civil_seguridad",
  "X02", "trafico_transporte",
  "X03", "proteccion_promocion_social",
  "X04", "salud_publica",
  "X05", "educacion",
  "X06", "urbanismo",
  "X07", "infraestructuras",
  "X08", "mantenimiento_urbano",
  "X09", "medio_ambiente",
  "X10", "cultura",
  "X11", "deportes_juventud_esparcimiento",
  "X12", "otros_bienes_sociales",
  "X13", "otros_bienes_economicos",
  "X14", "sectores_productivos"
)
categorias_nom <- categorias_inversion$categoria

archivos_inv_tipo <- list.files("../data/raw/inversiones_tipo_distrito", pattern = "^inv_tipo_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) # Looks within the folder for the file whose name exactly matches the pattern.
stopifnot(length(archivos_inv_tipo) == 21) # checks there are 21 files


# reads the files, function
leer_inv_tipo_archivo <- function(archivo) {
  distrito_nom <- str_remove(str_remove(basename(archivo), "^inv_tipo_"), "\\.csv$") # keeps the file path and strips out everything from the name except the district itself.
  distrito_key_archivo <- normalizar_nombre(str_replace_all(distrito_nom, "_", " ")) # replaces underscores with spaces and normalizes the district name

  read_csv(archivo, skip = 1, # skips the actual header and names the columns by hand
           col_names = c("anio", "id_linea", "nombre_linea", "inversion_detalle", "inversion_extra",
                         "presupuesto_gasto", "gasto_real"),
           col_types = cols(anio = col_integer(), id_linea = col_character(), nombre_linea = col_character(), inversion_detalle = col_character(), inversion_extra = col_character(), presupuesto_gasto = col_double(), gasto_real = col_double()), # defines the data types
           locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8")) %>% # sets the encoding

    filter(is.na(inversion_detalle) & is.na(inversion_extra)) %>% # only uses the rows that have the investment details empty in the raw file (NA in R) because those are the ones that give each category's total figure
    filter(anio >= 2017, anio <= 2023) %>%
    transmute(distrito_key = distrito_key_archivo, anio, id_linea, presupuesto_gasto, gasto_real)
}


# applies the function to the 21 files and stacks the results into a single table
inv_tipo_todos <- map_dfr(archivos_inv_tipo, leer_inv_tipo_archivo)

# joins by normalized name with the district catalog, bringing in distrito_num
inv_tipo_join <- inv_tipo_todos %>%
  left_join(distritos_norm_inv %>% select(distrito_key, distrito_num), by = "distrito_key")

# checks that no file name was left without a district and that all 21 distinct districts appear
stopifnot(sum(is.na(inv_tipo_join$distrito_num)) == 0)
stopifnot(n_distinct(inv_tipo_join$distrito_key) == 21)

# joins each row with the dictionary of the 15 categories, bringing in the readable name (categoria)
inv_tipo_cat <- inv_tipo_join %>% left_join(categorias_inversion, by = "id_linea")
stopifnot(sum(is.na(inv_tipo_cat$categoria)) == 0) # every id_linea must correspond to one of the 15 categories
```

#### To wide format and computing the indicator

```{r ancho 12}
# converts to wide format, with each category in its own column/variable
inv_tipo_ancho <- inv_tipo_cat %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, categoria, presupuesto_gasto, gasto_real) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = categoria, values_from = c(presupuesto_gasto, gasto_real), values_fill = 0)

# checks the number of rows
stopifnot(nrow(inv_tipo_ancho) == 21 * 7)
# checks the number of columns
stopifnot(ncol(inv_tipo_ancho) == 2 + 2 * length(categorias_nom))


# the denominator's total is Source 11's total investment (budgeted and actual)
inv_tipo_final_distrito <- inv_tipo_ancho %>%
  left_join(inversiones_distrito_pob %>% select(anio, distrito_num, presupuesto_gasto_distrito = presupuesto_gasto, gasto_real_distrito = gasto_real), by = c("anio", "distrito_num"))

# each mutate computes the % that each category represents of the total for its type (budget or actual spending)
inv_tipo_shares <- inv_tipo_final_distrito %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(paste0("presupuesto_gasto_", categorias_nom)), # every category of one type
                ~ .x / presupuesto_gasto_distrito,
                .names = "share_presupuesto_{sub('^presupuesto_gasto_', '', .col)}")) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(paste0("gasto_real_", categorias_nom)), # ...and of the other
                ~ .x / gasto_real_distrito,
                .names = "share_gasto_real_{sub('^gasto_real_', '', .col)}"))
```

#### Broadcast to neighbourhood

```{r broadcast 12}
barrios_sin_entidad_2017_inv2 <- c("183", "193", "194")  # 2017's missing neighbourhoods

# removes those neighbourhoods only when the year is 2017, the rest stays the same.
grid_barrio_anio_inv2 <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio) {
  base <- barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio)
  if (anio == 2017) base <- base %>% filter(!codigo_barrio %in% barrios_sin_entidad_2017_inv2)
  base %>% mutate(anio = anio, .before = 1)
})

# broadcast: since several neighbourhoods share the same district, each one of them receives the same investment-type % value from its district
inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio <- grid_barrio_anio_inv2 %>%
  left_join(inv_tipo_shares, by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

### Checks (02).

```{r gasto real}
# the actual-spending columns can indeed have NA (budget execution not reported in that category)
cols_gasto_real <- inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>%
  select(starts_with("gasto_real"), starts_with("share_gasto_real"))
sum(is.na(cols_gasto_real)) # there are 676 cells with NA

# is it because they haven't been reported in the most recent years? no, it's a consistent pattern.
inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(if_any(starts_with("gasto_real"), is.na)) %>%
  distinct(anio, distrito_num) %>%
  count(anio)

# are there some investment types whose budget executions are reported less often? Yes, especially in infrastructure and transport.
inv_tipo_final_distrito %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("gasto_real_"), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "categoria", values_to = "n_na") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_na))
```

```{r compro 12}
# checks NAs: no NA is expected in the budget columns - but they are expected in actual spending
cols_sin_na_esperado <- inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>%
  select(-starts_with("gasto_real"), -starts_with("share_gasto_real"))
stopifnot(sum(is.na(cols_sin_na_esperado)) == 0)

# checks the number of neighbourhoods per year
conteo_barrios_inv_tipo <- inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>% count(anio)
stopifnot(conteo_barrios_inv_tipo$n[conteo_barrios_inv_tipo$anio == 2017] == 128)
stopifnot(all(conteo_barrios_inv_tipo$n[conteo_barrios_inv_tipo$anio != 2017] == 131))

# checks there are no duplicate neighbourhoods
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio))) == 0)

# checks that the budget percentages cover 100% of the total
suma_shares_presu <- inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(suma = rowSums(across(all_of(paste0("share_presupuesto_", categorias_nom))))) %>%
  pull(suma)
stopifnot(all(abs(suma_shares_presu - 1) < 1e-6)) # == 1 with tolerance

# the actual-spending ones must also sum to 1, except in the district-years with some NA
gasto_real_cols_chk <- paste0("gasto_real_", categorias_nom)
suma_shares_real <- inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(tiene_na = if_any(all_of(gasto_real_cols_chk), is.na),
         suma = rowSums(across(all_of(paste0("share_gasto_real_", categorias_nom))))) %>%
  filter(!tiene_na) %>%
  pull(suma)
stopifnot(all(abs(suma_shares_real - 1) < 1e-6)) # == 1 with tolerance
```

### Saving


## Source 13: nationality by country of origin (`nacionalidad_pais_distrito.xlsx`)

**Dataset comments**:

District-level source. Builds the predictor "percentage of population born in countries with high or very high HDI" (≥0.700, the two upper brackets of the UNDP classification). The denominator used for the calculation is the district's total population (not the migrant population). Spain is excluded from the numerator since, even though it has a high HDI, the indicator seeks to capture transnational gentrification. `indice_desarrollo_humano.csv` is used, computing the classification separately for each year from that year's HDI. The source's 200 individual countries are all covered, but 13 are left without an iso3 since they are not countries with their own UNDP HDI

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 13, message=FALSE}
raw_nac <- read_excel("../data/raw/nacionalidad_pais_distrito.xlsx", sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE) # no header is assumed

geografias_txt <- as.character(unlist(raw_nac[6, 4:ncol(raw_nac)])) # stores the text of row 6 from column 4 to the end of the file -> where the district names are.

# parsing function for cleaning
parse_num_nac <- function(x) {
  x <- if_else(x == "..", NA_character_, x) # statistical-confidentiality sentinel
  as.numeric(str_remove_all(x, "\\.")) # removes the thousands separator
}


datos_nac_largo <- bind_cols( # rebuilds the full table starting from row 8 (where the data starts)
    raw_nac[8:nrow(raw_nac), 1:3] %>% set_names(c("fecha_txt", "grupo", "pais")), # renames the first three columns
    raw_nac[8:nrow(raw_nac), 4:ncol(raw_nac)] %>% set_names(geografias_txt) # fills in the columns with the district names extracted earlier
  ) %>%
  mutate(fecha_txt = as.character(fecha_txt)) %>%
  filter(str_detect(fecha_txt, "^1 de enero de \\d{4}$")) %>% # discards footer rows since they don't match that pattern
  mutate(anio = as.integer(str_extract(fecha_txt, "\\d{4}"))) %>% # rewrites the date as a year (the number only)
  filter(anio >= 2017, anio <= 2023) %>% # filters to the study window
  select(-fecha_txt) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(anio, grupo, pais), names_to = "geografia_txt", values_to = "valor_txt") # applies pivot_longer to make grouping easier later on


datos_nac_distrito <- datos_nac_largo %>%
  filter(geografia_txt != "Ciudad de Madrid") %>% # removes the city-total row
  mutate(distrito_num = as.integer(str_extract(geografia_txt, "^\\d{2}")), # extracts the district code
         valor = parse_num_nac(valor_txt)) %>% # applies parse_num_nac
  select(anio, distrito_num, grupo, pais, valor)

# checks there are no NAs
stopifnot(sum(is.na(datos_nac_distrito$distrito_num)) == 0)
# checks that the number of districts is 21
stopifnot(n_distinct(datos_nac_distrito$distrito_num) == 21)


# keeps the row where grupo=total and pais=total, since that row holds the population totals across nationalities for each district
total_poblacion_nac <- datos_nac_distrito %>%
  filter(grupo == "Total", pais == "Total") %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, poblacion_total_nac = valor)

paises_individuales_nac <- datos_nac_distrito %>% filter(grupo != pais) # excludes Total/España/Otro país/continent subtotals/Apátridas/No consta since those are the rows whose grupo-column text equals the pais-column text.
```

#### Classification of countries by HDI, year by year (`indice_desarrollo_humano.csv`)

```{r clasificacion 13}
idh_raw <- read_delim("../data/raw/indice_desarrollo_humano.csv", delim = ";",
                       locale = locale(encoding = "WINDOWS-1252"),
                       col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

idh_alto_anio <- idh_raw %>%
  filter(!str_starts(iso3, "ZZ")) %>% # discards the aggregate rows (development level/region/world, iso3 with "ZZ" prefix)
  select(iso3, starts_with("hdi_20")) %>%  # keeps iso3 and the columns starting with "hdi_20"
  pivot_longer(starts_with("hdi_20"), names_to = "anio", names_prefix = "hdi_", values_to = "hdi_txt") %>% # switches to long format so that country-year is one observation (specifies the prefix of what will become the names)
  mutate(anio = as.integer(anio), hdi = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(hdi_txt))) %>% # converts year and hdi values to numeric
  filter(anio >= 2017, anio <= 2023) %>% # filters to the study window
  transmute(iso3, anio, hdi, es_alto = !is.na(hdi) & hdi >= 0.700) # If NA or <0.700 = FALSE / if >= 0.700 = TRUE -> boolean flag to build es_alto (high-HDI value using the official threshold)

stopifnot(n_distinct(idh_alto_anio$iso3) == 195) # checks there are 206 rows in the csv - 11 aggregates = 195 countries
stopifnot(nrow(idh_alto_anio) == 195 * 7) # checks there are 195 countries for each of the years
```

### Broadcast to neighbourhood

```{r broadcast 13}
poblacion_idh_alto <- paises_individuales_nac %>%
  left_join(crosswalk_pais_iso3, by = "pais") %>% # joins paises_individuales_nac rows with their iso3
  left_join(idh_alto_anio %>% select(iso3, anio, es_alto), by = c("iso3", "anio")) %>% # also joins them with their HDI classification for that specific year
  filter(es_alto) %>% # discards countries that don't have a high HDI
  group_by(anio, distrito_num) %>%
  summarise(poblacion_idh_alto = sum(valor, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") # sums the population (ignoring NA).

# this left_join produces NA in case a district-year has no country with high HDI; when it appears in poblacion_idh_alto it should act as 0 (no population)
nacionalidad_idh_distrito <- total_poblacion_nac %>%
  left_join(poblacion_idh_alto, by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>%
  mutate(poblacion_idh_alto = replace_na(poblacion_idh_alto, 0),
         pct_poblacion_idh_alto = poblacion_idh_alto / poblacion_total_nac) # computes the indicator



barrios_sin_entidad_2017_nac <- c("183", "193", "194") # 2017's missing neighbourhoods
# removes those neighbourhoods only when the year is 2017, the rest stays the same.
grid_barrio_anio_nac <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio) {
  base <- barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio)
  if (anio == 2017) base <- base %>% filter(!codigo_barrio %in% barrios_sin_entidad_2017_nac)
  base %>% mutate(anio = anio, .before = 1)
})

# broadcast: since several neighbourhoods share the same district, each one of them receives the same % of high-HDI population value
nacionalidad_pais_distrito_barrio_anio <- grid_barrio_anio_nac %>%
  left_join(nacionalidad_idh_distrito %>% select(anio, distrito_num, # renaming
                                                   poblacion_total_distrito_nac = poblacion_total_nac,
                                                   poblacion_idh_alto_distrito = poblacion_idh_alto,
                                                   pct_poblacion_idh_alto_distrito = pct_poblacion_idh_alto),
            by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>% arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

## Source 14: green space by district (`zonas_verdes_distrito/`)

**Dataset comments**:

District-level source. Uses the surface area of "significant parks and green spaces" (sheet `ZV Y PARQUES SIGNIFIC. DISTRITO`), - motivated by De la Cruz & Ortín (2025). A normalized variable `zonas_verdes_significativas_m2_per_capita` (significant m² / district population) is computed.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 14, message=FALSE}
# reading per year
leer_zonas_verdes_significativas_anio <- function(anio) {
  archivo <- sprintf("../data/raw/zonas_verdes_distrito/zonas_verdes_%d.xlsx", anio)
  raw <- read_excel(archivo, sheet = "ZV Y PARQUES SIGNIFIC. DISTRITO")

  col_distrito <- names(raw)[str_detect(names(raw), "^DISTRITO$")] # looks for the column matching distrito
  col_ha <- names(raw)[str_detect(names(raw), regex("\\bha\\b", ignore_case = TRUE))] # looks for the column containing Ha: the surface area
  stopifnot(length(col_distrito) == 1, length(col_ha) == 1) # verifies that each search found one column

  raw %>% # table with two variables: district name and park hectares
    transmute(distrito_txt = .data[[col_distrito]],
              ha_parque = as.numeric(.data[[col_ha]])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(distrito_txt), !is.na(ha_parque)) %>% # keeps only the ones that do have values in both columns
    filter(!str_detect(distrito_txt, regex("total", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% # removes total rows
    group_by(distrito_txt) %>% # groups by district... to sum all the hectares
    summarise(zonas_verdes_significativas_ha = sum(ha_parque), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(anio = anio, .before = 1) # adds the year column
}

# applies the function to the 7 years and stacks the results into a single table
zonas_verdes_significativas_todos <- map_dfr(2017:2023, leer_zonas_verdes_significativas_anio)

zonas_verdes_significativas_join <- zonas_verdes_significativas_todos %>%
  mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(distrito_txt)) %>% # normalizes the district names (function already defined earlier)
  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% distinct(distrito_num, distrito_nombre) %>%
              mutate(distrito_key = normalizar_nombre(distrito_nombre)) %>% select(distrito_key, distrito_num),
            by = "distrito_key") # joins with barrios_madrid to bring in district identifiers
```

#### Normalization: m² per inhabitant

```{r per capita 14}
# computes the district population per year by summing all its neighbourhoods' population (uses tramo_edad_barrio_anio) -> denominator
poblacion_distrito_zv <- tramo_edad_barrio_anio %>%
  group_by(anio, distrito_num) %>%
  summarise(poblacion_total_distrito_zv = sum(poblacion_total_barrio), .groups = "drop")

# indicator computation
zonas_verdes_distrito_final <- zonas_verdes_significativas_join %>%
  select(anio, distrito_num, zonas_verdes_significativas_ha) %>%
  left_join(poblacion_distrito_zv, by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>% # joins the significant-park surface area with the district population
  mutate(zonas_verdes_significativas_m2_per_capita = zonas_verdes_significativas_ha * 10000 / poblacion_total_distrito_zv) # computation of m² per inhabitant / * 10000 converts hectares to m²
```

#### Broadcast to neighbourhood

```{r broadcast 14}
barrios_sin_entidad_2017_zv <- c("183", "193", "194") # 2017's missing neighbourhoods
# removes those neighbourhoods only when the year is 2017, the rest stays the same.
grid_barrio_anio_zv <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio) {
  base <- barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio)
  if (anio == 2017) base <- base %>% filter(!codigo_barrio %in% barrios_sin_entidad_2017_zv)
  base %>% mutate(anio = anio, .before = 1)
})

# broadcast: since several neighbourhoods share the same district, each one of them receives the same significant-green-space-per-capita value
zonas_verdes_distrito_barrio_anio <- grid_barrio_anio_zv %>%
  left_join(zonas_verdes_distrito_final %>%
              select(anio, distrito_num,
                     zonas_verdes_significativas_ha_distrito = zonas_verdes_significativas_ha,
                     zonas_verdes_significativas_m2_per_capita_distrito = zonas_verdes_significativas_m2_per_capita), by = c("anio", "distrito_num")) %>%
  arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

```{r compro 14}
# checks there are no NAs in the final table

# checks that the indicator is never negative

stopifnot(conteo_barrios_zv_sig$n[conteo_barrios_zv_sig$anio == 2017] == 128)

# correct broadcast: every neighbourhood within the same district-year shares the same value

  group_by(anio, distrito_num) %>%
  summarise(n_valores_distintos = n_distinct(zonas_verdes_significativas_ha_distrito), .groups = "drop")
```

## Source 15: distance to metro (`distancia_metro/`)

**Dataset comments**:

There are two files: `estaciones_metro_nodes.csv` (holds the stations with X/Y coordinates and their attributes), `itinerarios_metro_edges.csv` (holds the itineraries, the ordered sequence of stations and the distance to the previous station).

This variable is at neighbourhood level but has no year dimension since it is the current snapshot of the CRTM metro network. Using the current snapshot does not introduce much variation since the only modification completed and opened within the city of Madrid's limits between 2017 and 2026 was the creation of the Arroyofresno station (Line 7) in 2019. In the raw data there is an error in the Arroyofresno station's start date, which actually corresponds to April 2019, this being the only relevant metro-network modification. It will be accounted for through a manual correction in the years 2017 and 2018.

For every neighbourhood with a station of its own, the built variable represents the minimum number of segments (track segments between two consecutive stations of the same itinerary in a given direction) that must be traveled on the shortest path (measured in number of segments) from that station to Sol, treated as the reference "center" since it is kilometer zero of the Spanish radial highways. It is computed by building the metro network as a graph (stations = nodes; segments between consecutive stations = edges with weight 1 each, a transfer between lines at the same physical station = edge with weight 0, not counted as a traveled segment) and applying Dijkstra (via `igraph::distances()`) from Sol to the rest of the stations. There are 32 neighbourhoods that have no metro station of their own, so they are left with `paradas_red_centro` as NA.

### Reading and building the graph

```{r lectura 15, message=FALSE}
# reading
estaciones_raw <- read_csv("../data/raw/distancia_metro/estaciones_metro_nodes.csv",
                            col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                            locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))

itinerarios_raw <- read_csv("../data/raw/distancia_metro/itinerarios_metro_edges.csv",
                             col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                             locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))
```

```{r nodos 15}
# nodes
estaciones <- estaciones_raw %>%
  transmute(
    codigo_estacion = CODIGOESTACION, # renaming
    denominacion = DENOMINACION,
    nombre_norm = str_squish(stringi::stri_trans_general(str_to_upper(DENOMINACION), "Latin-ASCII")), # applies space cleanup, normalizes everything to uppercase, without accents, etc.
    municipio = CODIGOMUNICIPIO,
    distrito_metro = DISTRITO,
    barrio_metro = BARRIO,
    fecha_inicio = suppressWarnings(as.integer(str_sub(FECHAINICIO, 1, 4))), # keeps only the first 4 characters of the start date
    x = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(X)), # stores the coordinates as numeric
    y = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Y)))
```

```{r aristas de red 15}
# edges
itinerarios <- itinerarios_raw %>%
  transmute(codigo_itinerario = CODIGOITINERARIO, numero_orden = as.integer(NUMEROORDEN), codigo_estacion = CODIGOESTACION) %>%
  arrange(codigo_itinerario, numero_orden) # sorts the table by itinerary and then by stop order within that itinerary (each itinerary is a metro line traveled in one direction with its stops in order).

# creates the edges between two consecutive stations
tramos_red <- itinerarios %>%
  group_by(codigo_itinerario) %>% # groups by line-direction = itinerary
  mutate(codigo_estacion_previa = lag(codigo_estacion)) %>% # lag is a function that shifts a vector one position back, so it gives, in each row, the previous row's station within that same group. Each itinerary's first station has no "previous", so it will get NA.
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(codigo_estacion_previa)) %>% # discards each itinerary's first stop, since it has NA, as an edge cannot be created without an origin node.
  transmute(desde = codigo_estacion_previa, hasta = codigo_estacion, weight = 1) # assigned weight = 1
```

Interchange stations have a different CODIGOESTACION for each line passing through there. For the graph not to be split into per-line components, they need to be grouped.

```{r aristas de transbordo 15, warning=FALSE}
# transfers are detected by grouping by repeated normalized name:
grupos_nombre_metro <- estaciones %>%
  filter(!is.na(denominacion), denominacion != "", !is.na(x), !is.na(y)) %>% # filters out the ones without a name or coordinates
  add_count(nombre_norm, name = "n_estaciones_nombre") %>% # add_count: a dplyr shortcut that does group_by(nombre_norm) + row count per group + left_join() to the original table + ungroup() / the result is a new column with how many times that nombre_norm repeats across the whole table.
  filter(n_estaciones_nombre > 1) %>% # keeps the ones that repeat more than once
  select(nombre_norm, codigo_estacion, x, y)



# a self-join is done, joining grupos_nombre_metro with grupos_nombre_metro, in order to get every transfer combination
# Example with Sol: 3 rows with code S1, S2, S3. The join generates 3×3 = 9 combinations for that name (S1,S1), (S1,S2), (S1,S3), (S2,S1), (S2,S2), (S2,S3), (S3,S1), (S3,S2), (S3,S3)
transbordos_pares <- grupos_nombre_metro %>%
  inner_join(grupos_nombre_metro, by = "nombre_norm", suffix = c("_a", "_b")) %>% # since both copies of the table have the same columns, the _a and _b suffixes are added so as not to have two columns with the same name.
  filter(codigo_estacion_a < codigo_estacion_b) %>% # avoids duplicate pairs (S1,S3) vs. (S3,S1) and self-pairs (S3,S3) / it doesn't really evaluate < in a meaningful way but the condition works since it (arbitrarily) picks one of the two directions.
  mutate(distancia_m = sqrt((x_a - x_b)^2 + (y_a - y_b)^2)) # for each of those pairs computes the Euclidean distance between the two stations by directly applying the Pythagorean theorem to the coordinates


# builds a table with a weight-0 column, transfer origin and destination station
transbordos_edges <- transbordos_pares %>% transmute(desde = codigo_estacion_a, hasta = codigo_estacion_b, weight = 0)

# stacks the two edge tables vertically (one below the other) with their desde/hasta/weight columns
todos_los_tramos <- bind_rows(tramos_red, transbordos_edges)


# from the full station table, the ones with a known start date at or before 2023 are kept -> in practice this modifies almost no station.
estaciones_activas <- estaciones %>% filter(!is.na(fecha_inicio), fecha_inicio <= 2023)

# discards any edge that connects to a station excluded by the previous filter
tramos_activos <- todos_los_tramos %>%
  filter(desde %in% estaciones_activas$codigo_estacion, hasta %in% estaciones_activas$codigo_estacion)
```

```{r grafo 15}
# builds the GRAPH object
grafo_metro <- graph_from_data_frame(tramos_activos, # edges table
                                     directed = FALSE, # non-directional network
                                     vertices = estaciones_activas %>% # nodes table
               select(codigo_estacion)) 
```

### Shortest path from Sol

```{r desde sol 15}
# creates the node that will be used as the center reference

# keeps only the rows whose normalized name is exactly "SOL"
sol_codigos <- estaciones_activas %>% filter(nombre_norm == "SOL") %>% pull(codigo_estacion)
stopifnot(length(sol_codigos) == 3) # Sol has 3 codigoestacion values (lines 1, 2 and 3)


# creates the "CENTRO_HUB" node connected with weight 0 to Sol's 3 variants, in order to be able to ask igraph::distances() for a single origin
grafo_con_hub <- grafo_metro %>% # starts from the general graph
  add_vertices(1, name = "CENTRO_HUB") %>% # adds 1 node named CENTRO_HUB
  add_edges(c("CENTRO_HUB", sol_codigos[1], "CENTRO_HUB", sol_codigos[2], "CENTRO_HUB", sol_codigos[3]),
            weight = 0) # origin-destination vector (x3), each edge is added with weight 0 since it is a transfer


# computes the distance value from the center -> distances() computes the shortest-path distances from vertex v to every other vertex in the graph, using the weight vector.
paradas_desde_centro <- distances(grafo_con_hub, v = "CENTRO_HUB", weights = E(grafo_con_hub)$weight)[1, ]
# E(grafo_con_hub) is an igraph function that returns the graph's edge sequence, and $weight extracts the weight attribute for each of them
# [1, ] selects the matrix's first column (the only one there is) -> the 1st row starts from v and each column is one of the graph's vertices.


paradas_tbl <- tibble(codigo_estacion = names(paradas_desde_centro),
                      paradas_desde_centro) %>% # names is actually taken from the previous vector extracted with [1, ] which, coming from a matrix, keeps the original stop names as the names attribute.
  filter(codigo_estacion != "CENTRO_HUB") %>% # removed since it is not a real station itself
  mutate(paradas_desde_centro = if_else(is.infinite(paradas_desde_centro), NA_real_, paradas_desde_centro))
# Inf is what distances() returns for any vertex that cannot be reached from the origin -> in that case it is replaced with NA, and otherwise the same value is kept.

# checks that every active station is reachable from Sol
stopifnot(sum(is.na(paradas_tbl$paradas_desde_centro)) == 0)
```

### Aggregation to neighbourhood and broadcast to the study years

```{r neighbourhood 15}
estaciones_madrid <- estaciones_activas %>% # adds each active station's paradas_desde_centro value
  left_join(paradas_tbl, by = "codigo_estacion") %>%
  filter(municipio == "079" & !is.na(barrio_metro) & barrio_metro != "") # filters to only the ones in the city of Madrid (Madrid municipality) AND with a neighbourhood that is neither NA nor empty

# computes the distance to the neighbourhood -> picking the shortest path for each of them
distancia_barrio <- estaciones_madrid %>%
  rename(codigo_barrio = barrio_metro) %>%
  group_by(codigo_barrio) %>% # groups by the new codigo_barrio name
  summarise(paradas_red_centro = min(paradas_desde_centro), n_estaciones_metro = n(), .groups = "drop")
  # paradas_red_centro: minimum number of stops along the shortest path to Sol
  # n_estaciones_metro: how many metro stations that neighbourhood has within its boundaries

# neighbourhoods without any station of their own: NA in stops, 0 in number of stations
distancia_metro_barrio <- barrios_madrid %>% # starts from barrios_madrid and joins distancia_barrio to it -> this way all 131 are kept, and neighbourhoods with no match in distancia_barrio are left with NA
  left_join(distancia_barrio, by = "codigo_barrio") %>%
  mutate(n_estaciones_metro = replace_na(n_estaciones_metro, 0)) # replaces NA with 0 in n_estaciones_metro
```

```{r broadcast 15}
barrios_sin_entidad_2017_metro <- c("183", "193", "194") # 2017's missing neighbourhoods

# removes those neighbourhoods only when the year is 2017, the rest stays the same.
# runs the function for each year and stacks the results
distancia_metro_barrio_anio <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio_actual) {
  base <- distancia_metro_barrio
  if (anio_actual == 2017) base <- base %>% filter(!codigo_barrio %in% barrios_sin_entidad_2017_metro)
  base %>% mutate(anio = anio_actual, .before = 1)
})
```

### Manual correction of one neighbourhood

Arroyofresno is in the neighbourhood of Mirasierra with codigo_barrio "087". This neighbourhood has 3 other stations of its own (Pitis, Mirasierra, Paco de Lucía), so n_estaciones_metro should be 3 (not 4) in 2017 and 2018, and 4 from 2019 onward. As for paradas_red_centro, this column is not corrected since the minimum number of stops to Sol in that neighbourhood is determined by the Mirasierra station.

```{r correccion 15}
# investigates which station determines the minimum number of stops in the Mirasierra neighbourhood (087)
paradas_mirasierra <- estaciones_madrid %>%
  filter(barrio_metro == "087") %>%
  select(codigo_estacion, denominacion, paradas_desde_centro) %>%
  arrange(paradas_desde_centro)
paradas_mirasierra

minimo_con_arroyofresno <- min(paradas_mirasierra$paradas_desde_centro)
minimo_sin_arroyofresno <- paradas_mirasierra %>%
  filter(denominacion != "ARROYOFRESNO") %>%
  pull(paradas_desde_centro) %>%
  min()

# confirms that the minimum doesn't change if Arroyofresno is removed
stopifnot(minimo_con_arroyofresno == minimo_sin_arroyofresno)


# Manual correction for Arroyofresno
distancia_metro_barrio_anio <- distancia_metro_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(n_estaciones_metro = if_else(codigo_barrio == "087" & anio %in% c(2017, 2018), n_estaciones_metro - 1, n_estaciones_metro)) # if code 087 and years 2017-2018 hold, 1 station is subtracted, otherwise the same value is kept.
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 15}
# checks there is only 1 row per station in estaciones_raw (no duplicates)
stopifnot(n_distinct(estaciones_raw$CODIGOESTACION) == nrow(estaciones_raw))

# checks there are no NAs in tramos_red (edges)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(tramos_red$weight)) == 0)

# checks the number of edges for each itinerary (if an itinerary has n stops, it generates n−1 edges)
stopifnot(nrow(tramos_red) == nrow(itinerarios_raw) - n_distinct(itinerarios_raw$CODIGOITINERARIO))

# checks that at least some transfer was detected
stopifnot(nrow(transbordos_pares) > 0)

# checks the transfers with the greatest distance between their stations -> consistent with the Madrid metro.
transbordos_pares %>% slice_max(distancia_m, n = 5) %>%
  select(nombre_norm, codigo_estacion_a, codigo_estacion_b, distancia_m)

# checks that there are 99 neighbourhoods with a station of their own
stopifnot(sum(!is.na(distancia_metro_barrio$paradas_red_centro)) == 99)

# checks that the distance from Sol to itself is 0
stopifnot(distancia_metro_barrio$paradas_red_centro[distancia_metro_barrio$codigo_barrio == "016"] == 0)

# checks the number of neighbourhoods per year
conteo_barrios_metro <- distancia_metro_barrio_anio %>% count(anio)
stopifnot(conteo_barrios_metro$n[conteo_barrios_metro$anio == 2017] == 128)
stopifnot(all(conteo_barrios_metro$n[conteo_barrios_metro$anio != 2017] == 131))
```

## Source 16: Distance to the center (`geometria_barrios_extracted/`)

**Dataset comments**:

Two SHP files with the polygon of each Madrid neighbourhood, at two different dates: `data/raw/geometria_barrios_extracted/Barrios2017/Neighbourhoods.shp` and `data/raw/geometria_barrios_extracted/Barrios2021/Barrios_20210712.shp`. The variable doesn't offer much variance across years; nonetheless, 2017 and 2021 data (dates available from the Ayto. de Madrid data) were used to capture the administrative changes that affect a neighbourhood's shape and centroid location (Timón, Casco Histórico de Vicálvaro, Valdefuentes, Palomas and Alameda de Osuna).

Each neighbourhood's geometric centroid is computed and the straight-line (Euclidean) distance from that centroid to the centroid of the Sol neighbourhood (`016`) is measured, used as the "center" since it is kilometer 0 of the Spanish radial highways. Computing the distance from the neighbourhood's centroid was chosen for simplicity and because of its presence in the literature; however, the geometric centroid is not necessarily where people live. The coordinate system is the same in both (ETRS_1989_UTM_Zone_30N).

### Dataset cleaning

#### Computing the indicator in 2017 and 2021

The type of planar (x,y) coordinate system used by both 2017 and 2021 in their data is made explicit. The 2017 .prj file declares a compound CRS (with a vertical z component) that the polygon geometry doesn't actually use. It is homogenized with 2021 in order to compare centroids across the two dates without sf trying to reproject or failing due to a metadata mismatch.

```{r limpieza 16, warning=FALSE}
# 2017

barrios_shp_2017 <- st_read("../data/raw/geometria_barrios_extracted/Barrios2017/Barrios.shp",
                             options = "ENCODING=CP1252", quiet = TRUE)
st_crs(barrios_shp_2017) <- 25830 # ETRS_1989_UTM_Zone_30N

# computes each neighbourhood's centroid
barrios_centroides_2017 <- barrios_shp_2017 %>%
  mutate(centroide = st_centroid(geometry))

# determines the neighbourhood centroid used as the center reference in 2017: Sol
centro_ref_2017 <- barrios_centroides_2017 %>% filter(CODBAR == "016") %>% pull(centroide)

# computes the distance between the neighbourhoods' centroids and Sol's with st_distance
distancia_centroide_barrio_2017 <- barrios_centroides_2017 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(distancia_centro_lineal_m = as.numeric(st_distance(centroide, centro_ref_2017))) %>%
  select(codigo_barrio = CODBAR, distancia_centro_lineal_m) #CODBAR


# 2021
barrios_shp_2021 <- st_read("../data/raw/geometria_barrios_extracted/Barrios2021/Barrios_20210712.shp", quiet = TRUE)
st_crs(barrios_shp_2021) <- 25830 # ETRS_1989_UTM_Zone_30N

# computes each neighbourhood's centroid
barrios_centroides_2021 <- barrios_shp_2021 %>%
  mutate(centroide = st_centroid(geometry))

# determines the neighbourhood centroid used as the center reference in 2021: Sol
centro_ref_2021 <- barrios_centroides_2021 %>% filter(COD_BAR == "016") %>% pull(centroide)

# computes the distance between the neighbourhoods' centroids and Sol's with st_distance
distancia_centroide_barrio_2021 <- barrios_centroides_2021 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(distancia_centro_lineal_m = as.numeric(st_distance(centroide, centro_ref_2021))) %>%
  select(codigo_barrio = COD_BAR, distancia_centro_lineal_m) #COD_BAR
```

#### Broadcast to the study years (two segments)

The broadcast is done in parts: years 2017-2020 use the 2017 vintage, years 2021-2023 use the 2021 one. Since the 2017 shapefile has 131 neighbourhoods it can be used for the 2017-2020 period.

```{r diagnostico 16}
# diagnosis of the need for two segments when doing the broadcast -> some neighbourhoods change boundary (and therefore centroid) between 2017 and 2021

# investigates which neighbourhoods changed, comparing each neighbourhood's centroid in 2017 and 2021
comparacion_centroides <- barrios_centroides_2017 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(codigo_barrio = CODBAR, centroide_2017 = centroide) %>%
  left_join(barrios_centroides_2021 %>% # joins 2017 and 2021
      st_drop_geometry() %>%
      transmute(codigo_barrio = COD_BAR, centroide_2021 = centroide), by = "codigo_barrio") %>%
  mutate(desplazamiento_m = as.numeric(st_distance(centroide_2017, centroide_2021, by_element = TRUE))) # computes the distance between both years' centroids / by_element = TRUE makes it compare only the corresponding pairs row by row

# checks how many neighbourhoods have had their centroid shift by more than 10 meters, and it is only 4 neighbourhoods
# 10 meters is chosen to avoid capturing small digitization differences between versions
barrios_cambio_limite <- comparacion_centroides %>%
  filter(desplazamiento_m > 10) %>%
  pull(codigo_barrio)
barrios_cambio_limite

stopifnot(setequal(barrios_cambio_limite, c("214", "166", "161", "211")))
```

```{r broadcast 16}
# broadcast
# there are two map_dfr() calls applying the function, one for each segment, stacked together with bind_rows()
distancia_centro_lineal_barrio_anio <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(2017:2020, function(anio_actual) {
    distancia_centroide_barrio_2017 %>% mutate(anio = anio_actual, .before = 1)
  }),
  map_dfr(2021:2023, function(anio_actual) {
    distancia_centroide_barrio_2021 %>% mutate(anio = anio_actual, .before = 1)
  }))
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 16}
# checks that both shapefiles have 131 neighbourhoods and no duplicate codes
stopifnot(n_distinct(barrios_shp_2017$CODBAR) == 131)
stopifnot(n_distinct(barrios_shp_2021$COD_BAR) == 131)
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(barrios_shp_2017$CODBAR)) == 0)
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(barrios_shp_2021$COD_BAR)) == 0)

# checks that the universe of neighbourhood codes matches barrios_madrid in both years
stopifnot(setequal(barrios_shp_2017$CODBAR, barrios_madrid$codigo_barrio))
stopifnot(setequal(barrios_shp_2021$COD_BAR, barrios_madrid$codigo_barrio))

# confirms that both coordinate systems are projected (meters), not lat/long
stopifnot(st_is_longlat(barrios_shp_2017) == FALSE)
stopifnot(st_is_longlat(barrios_shp_2021) == FALSE)

# checks that the centroid falls within its own polygon in all 131 cases, in both years
stopifnot(all(st_within(barrios_centroides_2017$centroide, barrios_centroides_2017$geometry, sparse = FALSE) %>% diag()))
stopifnot(all(st_within(barrios_centroides_2021$centroide, barrios_centroides_2021$geometry, sparse = FALSE) %>% diag()))

# checks there are no NAs in both years
stopifnot(sum(is.na(distancia_centroide_barrio_2017$distancia_centro_lineal_m)) == 0)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(distancia_centroide_barrio_2021$distancia_centro_lineal_m)) == 0)

# checks the number of rows in the final table
stopifnot(nrow(distancia_centro_lineal_barrio_anio) == 131 * 7)

# checks that Sol gives distance 0 in both years
stopifnot(distancia_centroide_barrio_2017$distancia_centro_lineal_m[distancia_centroide_barrio_2017$codigo_barrio == "016"] == 0)
stopifnot(distancia_centroide_barrio_2021$distancia_centro_lineal_m[distancia_centroide_barrio_2021$codigo_barrio == "016"] == 0)

# checks that the broadcast is correct within each year segment (2017-2020 and 2021-2023)
chk_broadcast_centro_2017 <- distancia_centro_lineal_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(anio <= 2020) %>%
  group_by(codigo_barrio) %>%
  summarise(n_valores_distintos = n_distinct(distancia_centro_lineal_m), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(chk_broadcast_centro_2017$n_valores_distintos == 1))

chk_broadcast_centro_2021 <- distancia_centro_lineal_barrio_anio %>%
  filter(anio >= 2021) %>%
  group_by(codigo_barrio) %>%
  summarise(n_valores_distintos = n_distinct(distancia_centro_lineal_m), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(chk_broadcast_centro_2021$n_valores_distintos == 1))
```

## Source 17: unemployment rate (`tasa_paro.xlsx`)

**Dataset comments**:

This dataset is at neighbourhood level and in wide format. From this source only the absolute registered-unemployment-rate indicator, for December of each year, is needed.

### Dataset cleaning

```{r limpieza 17, message=FALSE}
raw_paro <- read_excel("../data/raw/tasa_paro.xlsx", sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE) # not assuming a header

# row 5 = fila_ciudad_paro carries the district name and the following row carries the district-total or specific-neighbourhood label
stopifnot(as.character(raw_paro[[5, 5]]) == "Ciudad de Madrid")
fila_ciudad_paro <- 5
col_ciudad_paro <- 5
etiquetas_geo_paro <- str_squish(as.character(unlist(raw_paro[fila_ciudad_paro + 1, col_ciudad_paro:ncol(raw_paro)])))

# keeps only the columns that have the neighbourhood pattern (3 digits + period) - discards "Ciudad de Madrid" and the 21 district-total columns
es_barrio_col_paro <- str_detect(etiquetas_geo_paro, "^\\d{3}\\.\\s") # 3-digit pattern
cols_barrio_paro <- (col_ciudad_paro:ncol(raw_paro))[es_barrio_col_paro]
barrio_txt_cols_paro <- etiquetas_geo_paro[es_barrio_col_paro]
stopifnot(length(cols_barrio_paro) == 131) # must be the 131 neighbourhoods



# cleaning function
parse_tasa_paro <- function(x) {
  x <- if_else(x == "..", NA_character_, x) # statistical-confidentiality sentinel becomes NA
  as.numeric(str_replace(x, ",", ".")) # rates use the European decimal comma (, is changed to .)
}

# locates the data rows: the first column carries the year as text (2017-2023)
filas_datos_paro <- which(str_detect(as.character(raw_paro[[1]]), "^\\d{4}$")) # the rows are the ones matching that year pattern
stopifnot(length(filas_datos_paro) == 7) # 2017-2023

tasa_paro_largo <- map_dfr(filas_datos_paro, function(f) { # builds the final table
  tibble(
    anio = as.integer(raw_paro[[f, 1]]),
    barrio_txt = barrio_txt_cols_paro,
    tasa_paro = parse_tasa_paro(as.character(unlist(raw_paro[f, cols_barrio_paro]))))
})


# join
tasa_paro_barrio_anio <- tasa_paro_largo %>%
  mutate(codigo_barrio = str_extract(barrio_txt, "^\\d{3}")) %>% # extracts the neighbourhood code
  left_join(barrios_madrid %>% select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio), by = "codigo_barrio") %>% # joins this table with barrios_madrid, bringing in the rest of the neighbourhood information
  select(anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, tasa_paro) %>% arrange(anio, distrito_num, barrio_num)
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro 17}
# checks that no codigo_barrio was left without finding its neighbourhood when joining with barrios_madrid
stopifnot(sum(is.na(tasa_paro_barrio_anio$barrio_nombre)) == 0)

# checks the number of neighbourhoods per year: 131 in all 7 years (this source doesn't have the 128-in-2017 exception, see the dataset comment)
stopifnot(all(count(tasa_paro_barrio_anio, anio)$n == 131))

# checks there are no duplicate neighbourhoods
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(tasa_paro_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio))) == 0)

# checks that 2017-2023 have no unexpected NAs
stopifnot(sum(is.na(tasa_paro_barrio_anio$tasa_paro)) == 0)
```

## Final union: complete neighbourhood-year panel

**Comments**:

The 16 thematic sources (Sources 2-17) are combined into a single neighbourhood-year panel. The final panel uses 131 neighbourhoods in 2017 since several sources do have real data for Ensanche de Vallecas/Valderrivas/El Cañaveral in 2017. As for column collisions between sources, the redundant copy is dropped before joining. This dataset includes variables that will ultimately not be used but were part of the construction/decision process.

```{r grid maestro}
# Builds the panel's skeleton/grid: 131 neighbourhoods x 7 years = 917 rows
panel_final_barrio_anio <- map_dfr(2017:2023, function(anio_actual) {
  barrios_madrid %>%
    select(distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio, barrio_oficial) %>%
    mutate(anio = anio_actual, .before = 1)
})
```

```{r union fuentes}
# a list of each source's objects
# before putting them in the list, the duplicate column is removed where applicable
tablas_a_unir <- list(
  composicion_hogares_barrio_anio,
  alquiler_barrio_anio,
  precio_vivienda_declarado_barrio_anio,
  rentas_barrio_anio,
  tramo_edad_barrio_anio,
  transacciones_vivienda_barrio_anio,
  panel_indicadores_barrio_anio,
  censo_locales_barrio_anio,
  churn_total_barrio_anio %>%
    select(-poblacion_total_barrio), # duplicate of tramo_edad
  inversiones_ayto_distritos_barrio_anio,
  inversiones_tipo_distrito_barrio_anio %>%
    select(-presupuesto_gasto_distrito, -gasto_real_distrito), # duplicate of inversiones_ayto
  nacionalidad_pais_distrito_barrio_anio,
  zonas_verdes_distrito_barrio_anio,
  distancia_metro_barrio_anio %>% select(-barrio_oficial), # already in the grid
  distancia_centro_lineal_barrio_anio,
  tasa_paro_barrio_anio)

# join loop
for (tabla in tablas_a_unir) {

  # before each join, the neighbourhood metadata columns already present in the grid are dropped
  tabla_limpia <- tabla %>%
    select(-any_of(c("distrito_num", "distrito_nombre", "barrio_num", "barrio_nombre"))) # any_of allows removing names that don't exist in every table without throwing an error
  panel_final_barrio_anio <- panel_final_barrio_anio %>%
    left_join(tabla_limpia, by = c("anio", "codigo_barrio"))

  # check
  cols_nuevas_sospechosas <- names(panel_final_barrio_anio)[str_detect(names(panel_final_barrio_anio), "\\.(x|y)$")] # detects whether there are columns with .x .y suffixes (duplicates)
  if (length(cols_nuevas_sospechosas) > 0) { # if those columns exist, it reports where and stops execution
    stop(sprintf("Unexpected column-name collision while joining this source: %s",
                 paste(cols_nuevas_sospechosas, collapse = ", ")))
  }}
```

### Checks (02).

```{r compro union}
# checks the panel's row count: 131 neighbourhoods x 7 years
stopifnot(nrow(panel_final_barrio_anio) == 131 * 7)

# the join keys (anio, codigo_barrio) must have no NA nor duplicates
stopifnot(sum(is.na(panel_final_barrio_anio$anio)) == 0)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(panel_final_barrio_anio$codigo_barrio)) == 0)
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(panel_final_barrio_anio %>% select(anio, codigo_barrio))) == 0)

# column count per source, to visually check that no entire source is missing
cat("Total number of columns in the final panel:", ncol(panel_final_barrio_anio), "\n")

# each table in the list is inspected before starting to join, in case any column carries the .x .y suffixes (which left_join uses when a column name is shared)
for (tabla in tablas_a_unir) {
  cols_sospechosas <- names(tabla)[str_detect(names(tabla), "\\.(x|y)$")]
  if (length(cols_sospechosas) > 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Found .x/.y columns (%s) -- rebuild this source (Restart R + Run All) before joining", paste(cols_sospechosas, collapse = ", ")))
  }}
```

### Saving

```{r save union}
write_csv(panel_final_barrio_anio, "../data/processed/panel_final_barrio_anio.csv")
```

```{r view union}
View(panel_final_barrio_anio)
```

## Final table with the selected variables

**Comments**:

This dataset is the closed selection of the index and predictor variables. `pct_hog_unipersonal_bajo65`, `pct_hog_monoparental` and `pct_hog_dos_adultos_sin_menores` are computed here from columns already present in `panel_final_barrio_anio`. `pct_extranjeros_ue_ocde`

```{r final}
dataset_modelado <- panel_final_barrio_anio %>%
  mutate(
    pct_hog_unipersonal_bajo65 = (hog_mujer_sola_16_64 + hog_hombre_solo_16_64) / total_hogares,
    pct_hog_monoparental = (hog_mujer_adulta_con_menores + hog_hombre_adulto_con_menores) / total_hogares,
    pct_hog_dos_adultos_sin_menores = hog_dos_adultos_sin_menores / total_hogares) %>%
  
  select(
    # identifiers
    anio, distrito_num, distrito_nombre, barrio_num, barrio_nombre, codigo_barrio,

    # index (6 dimensions that also enter as a t0-level predictor)
    pct_pob_25_39, nivel_estudios_superiores_pct, renta_neta_media_persona,
    pct_hog_unipersonal_bajo65, precio_vivienda_declarado_barrio,
    pct_extranjeros_ue_ocde,

    # predictors
    pct_hog_monoparental, pct_hog_dos_adultos_sin_menores,
    renta_colectiva_barrio,
    poblacion_total_barrio, tasa_transacciones_vivienda, densidad, tamano_hogar,
    envejecimiento, sobreenvejecimiento, pct_uso_vivienda,
    n_locales_activos_total, pct_comercio_menor, pct_turismo_alojamiento, pct_bares_restaurantes,
    pct_inmobiliarias, pct_arte_recreo_ocio, tasa_entradas_totales, tasa_salidas_totales,
    intensidad_inversion_real_distrito, share_gasto_real_urbanismo, share_gasto_real_mantenimiento_urbano,
    share_gasto_real_medio_ambiente, share_gasto_real_cultura, pct_poblacion_idh_alto_distrito,
    zonas_verdes_significativas_m2_per_capita_distrito, paradas_red_centro, n_estaciones_metro,
    distancia_centro_lineal_m, tasa_paro)
```

### Saving

```{r save final}
write_csv(dataset_modelado, "../data/processed/dataset_modelado.csv")
```
